title: OPERATION COLD MASONRY
skeleton: a relief force must clear a contested city core block by block to reach and extract a cut-off friendly element ringed by former comrades, against harassment built to slow and blind rather than stop, on a degrading hold-out clock where every hour late means more wounded and more wreckage to carry back out through ground that closes behind it
inspiration: the block-by-block urban clearance of Hue, 1968, crossed with the fight-out-to-extraction of Mogadishu, 1993
situation: A loyalist recon company on {WORLD} pushed too far into {DISTRICT} and went silent. {EMPLOYER} has the last known location: nine survivors and two crippled 'Mechs holed up in a grain-cooperative silo cluster near the old freight market. {TARGET_FACTION} troops now ring the position, and until a month ago those troops were on the same side. The district is packed masonry, three to six stories tall, with streets nine to fourteen meters wide. You cannot see more than two hundred meters in any direction. Your job is simple to say and hard to do: walk in, get the survivors out, and beat the closing ring. There is no air option. The buildings are too close and the anti-air fire is too heavy to land a relief lance on a rooftop. So you go in the only way a 'Mech can: on the ground, one block at a time, in the open. The defenders know this, and they have spent two days building traps along the approach. A hover platoon fires from a corner and vanishes before you can lock onto it. Mines in the rubble are set to blow under a 'Mech's weight. Snipers in the upper floors shoot at exposed crew and infantry, never at armor, because the goal is to make you fight closed-hatch and slow down. The last solid word from the trapped company is fourteen hours old and came in broken pieces over a dying radio. Their ammunition and water are both unknown. The troops holding the cordon are professionals who took the enemy's pay, and they will hold as long as the odds favor them. Every hour you spend reaching the silo means more wounded to carry and more wreckage to haul out.

objectives.primary: Reach the silo cluster and get the nine survivors and any recoverable 'Mech out before the cordon closes.
objectives.secondary: Keep the path you cleared open behind you, so the survivors are not forced to fight their way back out from a standing start.
objectives.bonus: Bring out both crippled 'Mechs instead of destroying them where they sit.

complications.name: The Vanishing Platoon
complications.text: A {TARGET_FACTION} hover platoon of five vehicles works the cross-streets ahead of you. It fires from a corner, then pulls back before you can lock on. This pulls your attention to one street while the cordon thickens on another. Chase it and you leave your route. Ignore it and it hits your flank when it hurts most.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The hover platoon moves to a new position every turn. Sending 'Mechs to chase it leaves your cleared path open to infiltration and adds one turn to the extraction clock.

complications.name: Weight-Triggered Rubble
complications.text: The defenders buried charges in the obvious lanes, set to blow under a 'Mech's weight. The clean, open street is the trap. The choked, slow one is safer. A tech can check the rubble for disturbed ground, but each check burns minutes, and you cannot see the enemy's clock.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Moving fast down the main streets risks a mine that cripples a leg. Moving carefully is safe but slower, and the extra time exposes the column to fire from the upper floors.

complications.name: Buttoned Up and Blind
complications.text: Snipers in the upper floors shoot at exposed crew and any infantry you brought. They never waste rounds on armor. The point is to force you closed-hatch, where you can only see what your sensors show you. In this tight masonry, that is very little.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Fighting closed-hatch cuts your spotting range and slows your reactions. Opening up to see better exposes crew to sniper fire and also slows the advance.

decisionPoints.name: The Line of Advance
decisionPoints.context: Two routes reach the silo cluster. The market boulevard is wide, so you can move fast and fight in the open. The interior alleys are slow and force single file in three spots, but they keep you hidden from the worst firing positions above.

options.title: Drive the boulevard
advantages: Fastest route to the trapped company
Open ground lets your 'Mechs fight at long range
Reaches the survivors before the cordon can double up
disadvantages: The boulevard is the street most likely to be mined
Long sightlines work both ways; the hover platoon can hit you from range
If a 'Mech loses a leg here, its wreck blocks your only way back out
options.consequence: You get there fast, but on the way back you fight through whatever the defenders moved in behind you.

costs.resource: Saves 3 turns on the extraction clock.
costs.risk: A mine on the boulevard cripples a 'Mech and blocks the escape route.

options.title: Thread the alleys
advantages: Hidden from the firing positions in the upper floors
The single-file chokepoints are easier to hold on the way out
Fewer buried mines in the tight lanes
disadvantages: Slow going; the trapped company loses hours it may not have
In single file, one stuck 'Mech halts the whole column
The close walls let enemy infantry rush in with satchel charges
options.consequence: You arrive late, and fewer survivors are left, but the path behind you is short and easy to hold.

costs.resource: Loses 2 turns on the extraction clock.
costs.risk: One stopped 'Mech in a narrow lane freezes the entire advance.

options.title: Split the axis
advantages: A fast element pins the hover platoon on the boulevard while the main body takes the alleys
Forces the cordon to split its attention
Keeps both routes open for the extraction
disadvantages: Splits a force that is already too small for the ground
The two groups cannot help each other once a building blocks their line of sight
If the timing slips, the enemy can crush each group one at a time
options.consequence: If the two groups stay in step, the cordon never closes. If they lose contact, one of them dies alone.

costs.resource: Requires 4 timing windows that must all hold.
costs.risk: If the two groups lose contact, the enemy masses on the weaker one.

decisionPoints.name: The Crippled 'Mechs
decisionPoints.context: The trapped company has two 'Mechs that cannot walk out on their own. Towing them costs time and ties up one working 'Mech per wreck. Leaving them means destroying valuable salvage in a war where every machine matters.

options.title: Tow them both out
advantages: Two 'Mechs recovered and returned to the line
Denies the enemy a rich salvage prize
The survivors keep the machines they fought for
disadvantages: A towing 'Mech is slow and cannot fight
Doubles the time you spend inside the cordon
If a tow breaks in the middle of a street, you lose the towing 'Mech too
options.consequence: You either bring everything home, or you turn a hard extraction into a disaster trying.

costs.resource: Loses 3 turns on the extraction clock.
costs.risk: A tow line snapping under fire strands two 'Mechs in the open.

options.title: Take one, scuttle one
advantages: Recovers half the salvage
Only one 'Mech is tied up towing
The 'Mech you destroy is left as a stripped wreck, not a prize
disadvantages: You still leave a valuable machine behind
Rigging and blowing the charges takes time and gives away your position
The crew of the destroyed 'Mech has to ride out as passengers
options.consequence: You keep moving at a bearable pace and accept the loss of one machine.

costs.resource: Loses 1 turn on the extraction clock.
costs.risk: The blast that destroys the 'Mech draws the cordon's heavy weapons onto the column.

options.title: Scuttle both, run light
advantages: Fastest possible extraction
No 'Mech tied up towing
Every gun stays free to fight
disadvantages: Two machines and their parts are lost to your own side, not just the enemy
The survivors lose 'Mechs they will be charged for
It looks bad on {EMPLOYER}'s salvage record
options.consequence: You get the people out fastest, then explain the wreckage to the quartermaster later.

costs.resource: Forfeits the salvage value of both 'Mechs.
costs.risk: The survivors' lost 'Mechs turn into a contract dispute.

entries.event: Your column crosses the freight-market line. The cordon's outer guards report contact.
The hover platoon starts its hit-and-run harassment along your route.
The defenders pull a reserve lance from the far side of the cordon and move it toward you.
The trapped company reports its last ammunition gone. From here they fight with sidearms and whatever they can throw.
The near side of the cordon has thickened so much that you can only leave by fighting your way out, not walking out clean.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: By T+3:30 the inner ring is so dense that any 'Mech still inside it either fights out over the bodies of the people it came to save, or does not get out at all.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced {TARGET_FACTION} company holding the cordon: 8-10 light and medium 'Mechs (25-55 tons, Regular, a Veteran command lance) built for the close fight - SRM and pulse-heavy, jump-capable. A combat-vehicle slice does the harassing: a hover platoon of 4-5 fast SRM/autocannon carriers (vehicleShare drives the mix) that fires and displaces. Mechanized infantry with mines and satchel charges color the streets but do not field as units. The cordon breaks contact on its own outer face if pressed past roughly 35% losses there, but tightens the inner ring rather than fleeing.
opforSketch.behavior: Disciplined cordon-and-squeeze. The defenders give ground on the outer edge so they can pack the inner ring tighter. They harass the relief force to slow it and blind it, and they refuse a stand-up fight they would lose. Their bet is that the clock kills the trapped company before you reach it.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN STREET
forks.trigger: The survivors and at least one 'Mech are extracted with the clearance corridor intact.
forks.consequence: The recovered company rejoins the line and {EMPLOYER} holds the district's freight quarter; the next move is to widen the corridor into a held sector before the enemy reforms.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL LADDER
forks.trigger: All nine survivors and both crippled 'Mechs come out, corridor held.
forks.consequence: A clean recovery; the salvage and the restored company let {EMPLOYER} mount a follow-on raid into the enemy's staging quarter while it is still off balance.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN MASON
forks.trigger: The cordon closes before extraction, or the clearance corridor is severed behind you.
forks.consequence: Whatever you brought in fights its own way back out through hostile blocks while the trapped company is overrun; the recovery becomes a withdrawal under pursuit.

storyElementSeed: A tech kneels in the rubble of a side street, reading the scuff-marks where someone buried a charge. Above her, a face appears in a cracked window and is gone before anyone can be sure it was there.

phases.name: APPROACH — THE OUTER BLOCKS
phases.lead: Cross the freight-market line and work your way toward the silo cluster. The enemy's harassment is built to slow you down and to figure out which way you are going.

routes.name: BOULEVARD
routes.desc: The market's wide, open main street.
routes.tradeoff: Fast and roomy, but the most heavily mined and the most exposed to long-range fire.

routes.name: INTERIOR
routes.desc: The tight alleys between the cooperative warehouses.
routes.tradeoff: Hidden and safer underfoot, but slow, and single file at three points.

sidebarKernel.kernel: which lanes show the disturbed ground of buried charges, and how many minutes a careful check of each one costs you.

phases.name: RELIEF — THE SILO CLUSTER
phases.lead: Reach the survivors. Take stock of who can move and what can move. Then decide what comes out and what stays behind.

dataBlock.Survivors: 9; two have wounds that can be treated in the field
dataBlock.Crippled 'Mechs: 2; one has a broken leg actuator, one a broken gyro. Neither can walk on its own
dataBlock.Survivor ammunition: Gone by T+2:00. Sidearms only after that
dataBlock.Tow capacity needed: 1 working 'Mech to tow each crippled machine

protocol.Recognition: Three long flashes of an amber work-lamp from the silo's loading dock. Answer the same way.
protocol.Backup contact: If you see no lamp within four minutes of arriving, send a short tightbeam burst with the codeword DRY HARVEST.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — THE WAY BACK
phases.lead: Move the recovered force out along the path you cleared. The cordon has had hours to thicken behind you.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether to fight the way back in leapfrogging rearguard bounds, or push everyone through in one mass before the inner ring closes.

assetDetails.detail: Still working as a unit, but worn out. The senior survivor will push to bring the crippled 'Mechs out and will resent any order to destroy them.
Salvage worth real money, but each one needs a working 'Mech to tow it and triples the time you spend in the kill-zone.

title: OPERATION SLOW WEATHER
skeleton: a counter-insurgent garrison must hold an insurgency below a contracted threshold across a whole season, where every heavy-handed sweep recruits for the enemy and every restraint reads as weakness, the population is both the shield and the only source of intelligence, and the posture chosen in the first weeks decides whether the season builds a peace or breeds a wider war
inspiration: the Briggs Plan and the clear-hold-build doctrine of the Malayan Emergency, 1948-1960
situation: The front line on {WORLD} collapsed, and the fighting left a mess behind it. {EMPLOYER} controls {DISTRICT} by day, but a {TARGET_FACTION} loyalist insurgency controls it after dark. It is a few dozen fighters with a handful of light 'Mechs hidden across the farm country. The farm towns feed and shelter these fighters, and you cannot tell which towns are on your side. Your contract is to pacify the district over one season. The hard part is that both ways of doing it backfire. Search homes hard to find fighters, and the anger you cause recruits more fighters. Leave fighters alone, and they plant the next mine under your supply road. The insurgents will not fight your 'Mechs head-on. They ambush, they hide their gear, and they blend into the farm crews. Their light 'Mechs appear for an hour to wreck a checkpoint, then get buried in a barn again by dawn. You have enough force to hold the district by force or to win its people over, but not both. Push the towns hard and the cells grow from the damage you cause. Go easy and the cells read it as weakness and attack more. Your intelligence comes from informers whose motives you cannot check, and their tips arrive about a day old. That is because the people who know where the caches are still have to live in these towns after you leave. There is no enemy front to push and no clear day you win. You just hold the line for a season, and every raid pushes the district toward a lasting peace or a wider war.

objectives.primary: Push {TARGET_FACTION} insurgent activity across {DISTRICT} low enough that it no longer threatens the main supply route. Then keep it that low for the whole contracted season.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the insurgency's hidden 'Mechs and their ability to replace them, without wrecking the towns that hide them.
objectives.bonus: Win a town over so fully that it hands you cache locations on its own, instead of giving them up only when you force it.

complications.name: The Reprisal Spiral
complications.text: Every rough sweep catches a few fighters, but it also makes people angry. Burned barns and jailed farmers give the cells their best recruiting tool. When you use force badly, you do the enemy's recruiting for them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each action that causes heavy collateral damage speeds up how fast the insurgency recruits fighters and replaces caches, for the rest of the season. A sweep that hits empty buildings does more harm than doing nothing.

complications.name: Informers With Two Faces
complications.text: Your tips come from people who still have to survive in the towns after your 'Mechs leave. Some give you old but real information. Some give you a rival's address to settle a grudge. Some send you into an ambush to prove their loyalty to the enemy. Every tip carries a hidden motive, so you can never fully trust one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every tip you act on has a hidden reliability roll. A bad tip either wastes a full sweep's worth of time or leads a patrol into a set ambush.

complications.name: The Hour of the Cached 'Mechs
complications.text: The cells hide two or three light 'Mechs in farm buildings. They bring them out only to hit a checkpoint, then vanish before your reaction force can reach them. To catch them, you have to already be where they appear. That means pulling forces away from somewhere else and leaving it weaker.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each cycle, insurgent 'Mechs hit a garrison point and pull back before your reaction force arrives. If you mass your forces to catch them, you leave another sector open to attack.

decisionPoints.name: The Posture of the Season
decisionPoints.context: How you garrison the district sets the whole campaign. This is not a tactical choice. It decides which kind of war you are fighting.

options.title: Cordon and search hard
advantages: Finds caches and fighters the fastest
Shows clear strength, which discourages open attacks
Gives an employer the quick body-count they want
disadvantages: Every empty house you search recruits more fighters
Turns the towns against you, drying up your informers
Leaves a stronger insurgency for the next garrison to face
options.consequence: You win the short-term numbers but lose the people. The cells then rebuild themselves from the anger you created.

costs.resource: the towns' goodwill, spent for good
costs.risk: collateral damage drives recruitment above the threshold you were hired to hold

options.title: Clear, hold, and build
advantages: Slowly cuts the cells off from the people who support them
Builds a strong informer network the cells cannot match
Leaves a district that stays quiet after you leave
disadvantages: Slow: attacks stay high for weeks before they drop
Ties your 'Mechs to guarding fixed points instead of attacking
Needs patience an employer watching weekly results may not have
options.consequence: The numbers look bad early and good later, but only if your employer lets the full season play out.

costs.resource: high enemy activity early in the season, which you must accept
costs.risk: an impatient {EMPLOYER} declares the contract failing before the numbers improve

options.title: Strike the cells, leave the towns
advantages: Hits fighters and caches directly using solid intelligence
Keeps collateral damage and public anger low
Protects the informer network by leaving the people alone
disadvantages: Only works if your intelligence is good, and it usually is not
A wrong strike on a bad tip becomes a public atrocity
Leaves the support network in place to rebuild the cells
options.consequence: Precise and clean when the intelligence is good, but a disaster the day it is wrong.

costs.resource: heavy reliance on your informer network
costs.risk: one strike on a false tip hands the enemy a massacre and a whole generation of recruits

decisionPoints.name: The Captured Cache
decisionPoints.context: A patrol finds a barn holding two insurgent 'Mechs and the families that hid them. How you treat these families decides whether that town gives you tips for the next month.

options.title: Detain everyone, make the example
advantages: Removes the people who keep the cache running
Shows other towns the price of hiding fighters
Produces interrogation leads, even if they are unreliable
disadvantages: Turns the whole town against you
The prisoners become a cause the cells rally around
Most of these people were forced to help, and the town knows it
options.consequence: The cache is gone, and so is any chance that town ever talks to you willingly.

costs.resource: one town's loyalty, lost for good
costs.risk: the arrests become the insurgency's main rallying cause

options.title: Take the 'Mechs, release the families
advantages: Takes away the cache without creating martyrs
Shows restraint the town will remember
Keeps your informer channel into that town open
disadvantages: Some of the people you release will hide the next cache
Looks weak to the fighters still out there
No interrogation leads, since you let everyone go
options.consequence: You lose the leads but keep the relationship, betting the town comes over to your side over time.

costs.resource: the interrogation leads you gave up
costs.risk: the people you released build a new cache somewhere else

options.title: Quietly turn one harborer
advantages: Places a source inside the support network
The town never learns the cache was betrayed from inside
Gives the best long-term intelligence of the three options
disadvantages: A source you forced to cooperate may turn on you
If the cell finds out, the source dies and the channel is ruined
Takes time and a handler who can never be traced back to you
options.consequence: If the source holds, you take the network apart from the inside. If the source is exposed, it costs a life and your credibility.

costs.resource: a handler who can never be traced back to you
costs.risk: if the source is exposed, they die and the town turns against you

entries.event: The season opens. You measure the starting level of insurgent activity across the district.
A cached 'Mech hits a checkpoint for the first time. Your reaction force reaches the area too late to catch it.
The posture you chose starts to visibly change how fast the insurgency recruits, up or down.
How exposed the supply route is becomes the number {EMPLOYER} watches. Activity near it now decides how your contract is judged.
Mid-season review. The trend you set in the first weeks is now the trend you are stuck with.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: By the end of the contracted season, district activity must be below the supply-route threshold and still falling. If it is not, {EMPLOYER} rules the pacification a failure and the next garrison inherits a war.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} loyalist insurgency, 40-60 fighters with 2-3 cached light 'Mechs (20-40 tons, Regular pilots in machines kept hidden between strikes) and a few improvised combat vehicles - converted farm haulers with bolted-on SRM and machine-gun mounts (vehicleShare colors the rare open fight). The 'Mechs come out only for hit-and-run strikes on garrison points and pull back before the reaction force arrives. They never fight a stand-up battle and break off the moment they are pinned. Foot fighters with mines and small arms are the constant threat but field narratively.
opforSketch.behavior: Standard guerrilla tactics: use small numbers to tie down a larger force. They hit soft targets, blend back into the farm population, and replace losses through the towns. The insurgency wins simply by surviving, and by goading the garrison into harsh reprisals that recruit more fighters for it.

forks.name: OPERATION FAIR HARVEST
forks.trigger: District activity falls below the supply-route threshold and the towns are tilting toward cooperation by season's end.
forks.consequence: The district stabilizes and {EMPLOYER} extends the garrison's writ; the next operation is rolling up the now-isolated cells before they can regroup.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY ROT
forks.trigger: A town volunteers cache locations and the insurgency's 'Mech capability is broken without a razed village.
forks.consequence: The insurgency collapses from within; the freed-up force can be redeployed to a contested district that needs it more.

forks.name: OPERATION HARD FROST
forks.trigger: Heavy-handed sweeps spike recruitment and the supply route comes under sustained attack.
forks.consequence: The insurgency grows past containment; what was a pacification becomes a fight to keep the main route open at all, with the towns now solidly hostile.

storyElementSeed: A patrol leader stands in a farmyard at dawn. He holds a tip that names this house, but the family in front of him has done nothing he can prove. He has to decide whether the war he is really fighting is the one his orders describe.

phases.name: POSTURE — OPENING THE SEASON
phases.lead: Set the garrison's stance across the district. Accept that the choices you make in the first weeks shape the whole campaign.

dataBlock.District towns: 11, ranging from hostile to cautiously neutral
dataBlock.Supply-route length: the number {EMPLOYER} watches to judge the contract

sidebarKernel.kernel: how old each informer's tips tend to be, and which towns have started talking versus which have gone quiet.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE CACHE AND THE TOWN
phases.lead: A patrol finds a 'Mech cache and the families that kept it running. The choice you make here shapes how the whole district feels about you for weeks.

protocol.Informer contact: Messages are left in a hidden spot at the grain exchange. A chalk mark on the north post signals a drop is waiting.
protocol.Reaction call: The codeword SLOW WEATHER sends the nearest reaction lance to a checkpoint that is under attack.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE TREND YOU OWN
phases.lead: Ride out the season on the trend you set, working to push activity below the threshold before the assessment date.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the trend is heading toward a quiet district or a wider war, and what one more month would cost either way.

assetDetails.detail: Runs the informer network. Warns that about half the tips are people settling private grudges, and that pushing the network too hard will make it collapse.
Each town leans toward you or against you based on how the garrison treats it. Goodwill spent on one sweep does not come back, and a single atrocity turns all of them against you.

title: OPERATION LONG SHADOW
skeleton: a covering force must delay an advancing battalion across successive phase lines to buy a helpless column its withdrawal time, deliberately losing every stand while never letting itself be fixed, against a fix-and-flank enemy and a required-delay clock that keeps growing as the column lags, spending its own strength on ground that means nothing except as time
inspiration: covering-force delay doctrine and the phase-line withdrawal fighting of Lorraine, 1944
situation: You are ordered to give ground, not hold it. {EMPLOYER}'s main body on {WORLD} is pulling out of {DISTRICT}. It is a slow column of dropships, repair vehicles, and families. It needs three days of clear road to reach its new line, and it cannot fight while it moves. Your company is the covering force. Your job is not to win. Your job is to buy the column those three days. A reinforced {TARGET_FACTION} battalion is pushing into the district behind a fast scout screen. You must force that battalion to stop, spread out, and fight for ground you do not care about keeping. Here is the method. You set up on a phase line, which is a mapped stop line. You make the enemy think you plan to hold it. You hurt his lead units. Then you fall back to the next line before he can pin you in place. You repeat this at each line, giving up the district one ridge at a time. Losing each stand is fine, because you are meant to lose each stand. The real danger is staying too long. If the enemy's main weight pins you against the terrain, your company gets destroyed. If the covering force dies, the column behind it is caught in the open with no shield. One more problem: the estimate of how fast the enemy moves is only a guess, and guesses about an aggressive enemy tend to be too hopeful. Behind you the column crawls. Ahead of you a battalion wants to shove you aside and reach it. You have three days to keep blocking without ever getting caught.

objectives.primary: Slow the {TARGET_FACTION} advance through {DISTRICT} for about three days. That is how long {EMPLOYER}'s main body needs to clear the district and reach its new line.
objectives.secondary: Keep your covering force strong enough to still fight when it reaches the last stop line.
objectives.bonus: Hurt the enemy's lead units so badly that they slow down and become cautious. A cautious pursuit gives the column even more time than it needs.

complications.name: The Fix-and-Flank
complications.text: The enemy has a set plan against a delay. Their scout screen pins you in front while their main force swings wide to cut off the road you plan to retreat on. Every time you hold a stop line too long, you give them time to get behind you. Your key job is to spot the moment they start that flanking move, so you can pull back before the road is cut.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If you hold a stop line past its safe timing window, an enemy flanking force may reach your retreat road. Once that happens, pulling out costs you losses instead of just time.

complications.name: The Optimistic Clock
complications.text: Your estimate of how fast the column moves and how fast the enemy advances is only a guess, and the guess tends to be too hopeful. If the column falls behind or the enemy pushes harder than expected, you have to buy more time with fewer units than you planned for.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The amount of time you must buy can grow partway through the operation. Each phase, a column-progress report tells you whether you are ahead of or behind schedule.

complications.name: Terrain That Runs Out
complications.text: There is only so much good ground to delay on. Ridges, narrow passes, and river lines run out. The first stop lines are strong. The last ones are open farmland with nothing to hide behind. So the further back you fight, the harder each stand becomes.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each stop line gives you less protection than the one before it. Fighting on the open rear lines costs far more of your covering force than fighting on the strong forward ones.

decisionPoints.name: How Hard to Hold the Line
decisionPoints.context: At each stop line, you choose how hard to fight before you pull back. Fighting harder buys more time but costs more of your force. You cannot afford to get this wrong twice.

options.title: Heavy stand, maximum delay
advantages: Buys the most time at each stop line
Convinces the enemy you mean to hold, which slows their whole advance
Does real damage to the enemy's lead units
disadvantages: Highest risk of being pinned in place and outflanked
Uses up force you will need for the later stop lines
If the stand goes wrong, you can lose both the company and the column
options.consequence: You buy the column hours, but you gamble that you spot the flanking move in time to pull out.

costs.resource: Time bought: high. Force spent: high.
costs.risk: Staying too long lets a flanking force cut your retreat road and trap the company.

options.title: Light contact, quick displacement
advantages: Saves your force for the stop lines that matter most
Low risk of being pinned in place
Keeps the company quick and mobile across the whole district
disadvantages: Buys little time at each line
Looks weak, so the enemy pushes faster
May not add up to the total delay the column needs
options.consequence: You keep your force intact, but you risk not buying enough time to matter.

costs.resource: Time bought: low. Force saved: high.
costs.risk: The column reaches its line late and is caught while still moving.

options.title: Feint a stand, then ambush the pursuit
advantages: Looks like a real stand, then hits the enemy hard when he charges in
A hurt lead force advances more slowly, buying extra time
Costs you ammo and position rather than your whole force
disadvantages: Hard to time under pressure; get it wrong and it becomes a real stand by accident
Works only once or twice before the enemy stops falling for it
Needs terrain with both an open front to show and cover to hide a flank
options.consequence: Done right, it buys time cheaply and makes the enemy cautious. Done wrong, it turns into the heavy stand you were trying to avoid.

costs.resource: Ambush ground: you need terrain that fits.
costs.risk: A botched ambush leaves your force half-committed and out of position.

decisionPoints.name: The Lagging Column
decisionPoints.context: Word comes that the main body is behind schedule, so the time you must buy has grown. You have three choices. Spend more of your force to buy the extra time. Gamble that the enemy slows down on his own. Or sacrifice a small element to guarantee the rest of the column gets clear.

options.title: Spend the force, buy the time
advantages: Guarantees the column the extra hours it now needs
Protects the families and wounded riding in the column
Delivers exactly what the mission is for
disadvantages: May wreck your covering force before it reaches the final line
Turns a survivable delay into a costly one
Leaves you weak if the enemy still has fresh units to push with
options.consequence: The column gets clear, and your covering force pays for it in lost machines and crews.

costs.resource: Covering-force strength: heavily spent.
costs.risk: The company reaches the final line too weak to hold it.

options.title: Bet the enemy culminates
advantages: Saves your force, betting the enemy advances faster than his supplies can follow
An aggressive pursuit often does outrun its own supply lines
Keeps your options open if the bet pays off
disadvantages: You are betting on the enemy's supply state, which you cannot see
If you are wrong, the column is caught and you did nothing to stop it
Hands the initiative fully to the enemy
options.consequence: If the enemy slows on his own, you save your force at no cost. If he does not, the column pays for your gamble.

costs.resource: Force saved, but only if the supply gamble pays off.
costs.risk: The enemy pushes through and catches the column in the open.

options.title: Sacrifice a rearguard element
advantages: A small holding force buys guaranteed time while the rest stays mobile
Puts the loss on one element instead of risking the whole company
Buys a clean getaway for the main covering force and the column
disadvantages: The rearguard element is likely lost or captured
You are trading a few crews so the rest survive
A hard order to give and a harder one to live with
options.consequence: The column and most of the company get clear. The rearguard holds until it cannot, and you carry that.

costs.resource: One rearguard element: written off.
costs.risk: The sacrificed element is overrun before it buys the full time window.

entries.event: The covering force sets up on the first stop line. Behind it, the column starts moving.
The enemy scout screen makes contact. Behind it, the lead battalion starts spreading out to fight.
You fall back from the first line. The enemy pushes, testing whether you meant to hold it or just delay.
A column-progress report arrives. Now you learn how much time you really have to buy, whether the early guess was too hopeful or not.
The covering force falls back to the last, weakest lines. The enemy commits his main weight to finish it off.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: By the end of day three, one of two things is true. Either the main body has cleared the district and reached its new line, or your covering force has been pinned and the column is caught in the open because the time ran out.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced {TARGET_FACTION} battalion pushing forward to find and fight you. A fast scout screen of light 'Mechs and hover/wheeled scout vehicles leads the way (vehicleShare carries the screen and a tracked support slice). Behind it comes the main body: 24-30 medium and heavy 'Mechs (40-75 tons, Regular quality with a Veteran spearhead). The screen finds you and pins you in place; the main body spreads out to swing around your flank. The lead element pushes hard, but it turns cautious once hurt, and it will break off a pursuit that costs it more than roughly 25% of the lead company.
opforSketch.behavior: Aggressive. The enemy pushes forward to make contact, then pins your front with the screen while the main body swings around to cut off your retreat, trying never to let you break away clean. But that aggression is also his weakness: an over-eager pursuit is the covering force's best weapon against him.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR ROAD
forks.trigger: The main body clears the district and the covering force reaches the final line still fighting.
forks.consequence: The reposition succeeds and the covering force rejoins the new line intact; {EMPLOYER} sets a fresh defense with its formation whole.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN SPEAR
forks.trigger: The enemy's lead element is bloodied badly enough that the pursuit goes timid and over-delivers time.
forks.consequence: The covering force comes off the field nearly intact and the enemy advance stalls cautious; {EMPLOYER} can counterattack into an over-extended pursuit.

forks.name: OPERATION CAUGHT IN THE OPEN
forks.trigger: The covering force is fixed and overrun, or the delay falls short and the column is caught moving.
forks.consequence: The main body takes the hit it was meant to be spared; survivors of the covering force fight a disorganized withdrawal to whatever line still holds.

storyElementSeed: Through field glasses, a company commander watches the column's dust thin out behind her. Then she turns to the ridge ahead and counts the minutes she can hold before holding gets her killed.

phases.name: SCREEN — THE FIRST LINES
phases.lead: Set up on the strong forward stop lines. Make the enemy spread out to fight you, hurt his lead units, then fall back on your own timing before he can pin you.

dataBlock.Phase lines available: 5 stop lines, strongest in front and open ground in the rear
dataBlock.Required delay: about 3 days (only a guess, and it tends to be too hopeful)
dataBlock.Covering force: one company; must never let itself get pinned in a full fight
dataBlock.Column composition: dropships, repair vehicles, and families - cannot fight while moving

sidebarKernel.kernel: how fast the enemy is actually moving compared to the guess, and the first sign that a flanking force is starting its move.

phases.name: DELAY — TRADING THE DISTRICT
phases.lead: Fall back one line at a time. Hold each line just long enough, and watch for the flanking move that can turn a delay into a trap.

routes.name: RIDGE LINE
routes.desc: High-ground delay positions that can cover each other with fire.
routes.tradeoff: Strong to defend, but it is the obvious route, so the enemy scouts it first.

routes.name: RIVER DEFILES
routes.desc: The narrow river crossings between the stop lines.
routes.tradeoff: Great for a fast, hard hit, but a force caught with its back to the water cannot pull out cleanly.

protocol.Displacement order: Codeword LONG SHADOW means abandon a stop line. Units then fall back past each other to the next line.
protocol.Flank warning: Codeword OPEN GATE means an enemy flanking force has reached your retreat road. Break contact now, or get cut off.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE LAST GROUND
phases.lead: Fight the final, weakest lines while the column finishes clearing the district. Then decide how much your covering force is willing to spend in these last hours.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the column has cleared yet, and whether your force has one more delay in it or has to break for the new line now.

assetDetails.detail: Slow, mixed, and helpless while it moves. How fast it travels is the real clock, and it falls behind more often than it runs ahead.
It gets weaker with every fight, but it must still be able to fight at the final line. Every line you hold too long costs strength you will need later.

title: OPERATION FALSE WEIGHT
skeleton: a demonstration force must make a feint dangerous and convincing enough to pull an enemy mobile reserve off the real objective and hold it committed until the main effort lands, then break contact in the narrow window between the main effort's commitment and the freed reserve turning to hunt the demonstrator with a battalion's weight and a grudge
inspiration: the operational deception of Operation Bodyguard, 1944 - a demonstration-in-force that fixes the enemy's reserve
situation: The real attack lands two hundred kilometers away. Your company is here to make sure {TARGET_FACTION} is looking the wrong way when it does. {EMPLOYER} plans to seize the river crossings at the far end of {DISTRICT}. The one thing that can stop that is the enemy's mobile reserve, a heavy battalion sitting in the center, ready to swing toward whichever threat looks real. Your job is to be the threat that looks real. You will attack a secondary target hard enough, and put on enough visible force and convincing aggression, that the reserve commits to you and pulls away from the crossings. Here is the hard part. The fake attack only works if it is truly dangerous. That means fighting a full battalion with only a company, and keeping up the fight until the moment the real attack goes in and the enemy realizes he guarded the wrong place. Then that entire battalion turns on you with nothing else to do but hunt you down. You will learn the real attack has started from a scheduled time you have to trust, sent over a comms plan that assumes the enemy is jamming your radios. Push too softly and the reserve hedges its bets and splits its force, so the crossings cost more to take than they should. Push too hard and stay too long, and you are one company that picked a fight with a battalion and got caught when the trick stopped working. The enemy only shifts his reserve if he believes you are stronger than you really are.

objectives.primary: Pull {TARGET_FACTION}'s mobile reserve away from the river crossings and keep it focused on you until the real attack has gone in.
objectives.secondary: Break contact and pull your company out cleanly once the fake attack has done its job.
objectives.bonus: Hold the reserve so completely that the crossings fall before it can even turn back to help.

complications.name: Conviction Has a Price
complications.text: A fake attack the enemy can shrug off is worthless. To pull a whole battalion, you have to commit real force, take ground, and accept fights a raid would dodge. The feint has to visibly cost you something, or nobody believes it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The harder you press, the more of its reserve the enemy commits to you. A cautious fake attack leaves the reserve hedging and still partly guarding the real target.

complications.name: The Turning Battalion
complications.text: The moment the enemy sees the real attack, the reserve stops reacting to you and starts hunting you, with a full heavy battalion and a score to settle. The clean pullout you planned now happens against a force that wants to destroy you.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When the real attack goes in, the enemy switches from cautious to full aggressive pursuit. The longer you wait to break contact, the deeper your company is when that switch happens.

complications.name: Jammed Timing
complications.text: The signal that the real attack has started comes over a comms plan built to survive enemy jamming. So it may arrive late, garbled, or only on a backup channel you have to be listening for. The two ways to fail are acting on a false signal, or missing the real one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The signal to break contact may be late or unclear. Break too early and you waste the feint. Break too late and the company is caught by the reserve as it turns on you.

decisionPoints.name: How Loud to Be
decisionPoints.context: How hard you press the fake attack decides everything. Press hard and the reserve commits fully, but you are deep in the fight when it turns on you. Press lightly and you stay safe, but the reserve may not take the bait.

options.title: Full demonstration
advantages: Pulls the reserve completely off the crossings
Gives the real attack the cleanest run at them
Sells the fake attack beyond any doubt
disadvantages: Your company is deep in the fight when the enemy battalion turns on you
You take the heaviest losses pulling out
You have no room to spare if the go signal arrives late
options.consequence: The crossings fall easily, but pulling your company out is the hardest part of the day.

costs.resource: You commit as hard as you can, holding nothing back.
costs.risk: The enemy battalion turns and catches your company too far forward to pull out.

options.title: Measured pressure
advantages: Keeps your company in control so you can pull out cleanly
You take fewer losses the whole way through
Still convincing if the terrain makes your force look bigger than it is
disadvantages: The enemy battalion may hold back instead of fully committing to you
A battalion that holds back still keeps part of its force guarding the crossings
The main attack then has to fight the part of the battalion that stayed behind
options.consequence: You come through in good shape, but the main attack pays part of the price you were meant to cover.

costs.resource: The enemy battalion only partly commits to you.
costs.risk: The crossings cost the main attack more because the battalion never fully left.

options.title: Inflate the picture
advantages: Uses dust, fake radio signals, and spread-out movement to look like two companies
Pulls the enemy battalion while risking less of your real force
Gives the best result for the fewest losses, as long as the trick holds
disadvantages: If enemy scouts get a close look, the bluff falls apart at once
You need the right terrain and tight discipline to keep the illusion going
If the enemy sees through it, the battalion attacks you and still guards the crossings
options.consequence: If the enemy believes the bluff, you win cheaply. If his scouts see through it, you fail at both goals.

costs.resource: You spend decoy transmitters and rely on tight unit discipline.
costs.risk: Enemy scouts see through the bluff and the fake attack falls apart.

decisionPoints.name: When to Break
decisionPoints.context: The go signal is late and hard to read. You can pull out on the planned time, pull out on the unclear signal, or wait for a clear confirmation. Each choice is a gamble on the jamming and on how the enemy is reading your force.

options.title: Break on the schedule
advantages: You pull out while the enemy battalion is still focused on you, not yet turning
This gives the cleanest getaway of the three choices
It follows the plan and trusts the main attack hit its window
disadvantages: If the main attack ran late, you ended the fake attack too early and freed the enemy battalion
You are trusting the clock over the actual signal
The crossings may be left open to a battalion that never fully committed
options.consequence: You get out cleanly, betting the main attack went in on time.

costs.resource: You get a clean, low-loss withdrawal.
costs.risk: Pulling out too early frees the enemy battalion before the crossings are taken.

options.title: Break on the ambiguous signal
advantages: You act on the best read you have of when the main attack went in
It balances how long you keep the fake attack going against staying alive
If the signal is real, this best matches the true moment to pull out
disadvantages: The signal may just be noise from the jamming or a broken fragment
A wrong read ends the fake attack at the worst possible moment
It splits the difference and may fail to do either job well
options.consequence: You act on the unclear signal, knowing it might be wrong.

costs.resource: You make a judgment call on a garbled radio signal.
costs.risk: The signal was false, so you either pull out into a battalion still watching you, or you hold while it turns on you.

options.title: Hold for hard confirmation
advantages: Makes sure the fake attack does its full job
You can not pull out too early and leave the crossings open
It keeps the enemy battalion off the main attack for as long as possible
disadvantages: Clear confirmation may not arrive until the enemy battalion is already turning on you
This is the deepest, most costly pullout of the three choices
It bets your whole company on the crossings being worth the price
options.consequence: The main attack gets every minute it needs, and your company pays for those minutes on the way out.

costs.resource: You spend your company's safety margin to help the main attack.
costs.risk: The confirmation arrives only after the enemy battalion is already on top of you.

entries.event: You open the fake attack on the secondary target. The enemy command starts sizing up the threat.
Enemy scouts probe your force to work out how strong you really are.
The enemy battalion starts moving toward you, away from the crossings. If the fake attack was weak, it only partly commits.
This is the planned time the main attack goes in. The go signal is due over the jam-resistant radio plan.
Once the enemy sees the main attack, the battalion breaks off and turns to hunt your company.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Pull out before the turning battalion pins your company. Once it turns back on you, you have only minutes to break clean, and a company caught by a heavy battalion rarely survives.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} mobile reserve, a heavy battalion: 24-32 medium and heavy 'Mechs (45-80 tons, Regular with a Veteran command company), backed by a fast combat-vehicle screen and a tracked fire-support slice (vehicleShare carries the scouts and gun carriers). The battalion is held ready to react to either threat and commits only once it is sure which one is the real attack. It probes first, then commits. Once it spots the real attack, it turns and chases hard, pressing a force that is trying to pull out.
opforSketch.behavior: The battalion holds back and refuses to move until it is sure which attack is real, then throws its full weight at that one. Your fake attack has to overcome the commander's caution to pull him in. Then, when he turns on you, your company has to survive his hard pursuit.

forks.name: OPERATION FAR CROSSING
forks.trigger: The reserve commits to the feint, the main effort takes the crossings, and the company breaks contact intact.
forks.consequence: The crossings fall and the company rejoins {EMPLOYER}; the next move exploits the bridgehead the reserve failed to defend.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY CENTER
forks.trigger: The reserve commits so fully it cannot re-orient, and the crossings fall before it turns at all.
forks.consequence: The reserve is left stranded and out of position; {EMPLOYER} exploits an enemy center scraped clean of its mobile weight.

forks.name: OPERATION WRONG HORSE
forks.trigger: The feint is seen through, or the company is caught by the turning reserve before it can break.
forks.consequence: The crossings cost the main effort dearly against a reserve that never left, and the demonstration force fights a costly withdrawal under a battalion's pursuit.

storyElementSeed: A radio operator leans over a receiver full of jamming static, trying to catch one clear word. The company commander watches her, waiting for a nod that means run or stay.

phases.name: OPENING — SELLING THE THREAT
phases.lead: Open the fake attack with enough visible force and aggression that the secondary target looks like the real one.

dataBlock.Demonstration force: your one company, made to look bigger
dataBlock.Target reserve: one heavy battalion, held in the center, ready to react
dataBlock.Main effort: the river crossings, about 200 km away
dataBlock.Go signal: sent at a set time over a jam-resistant radio plan

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the enemy battalion is committing to you or holding back, and what its scouts have worked out about your real strength.

phases.name: FIXING — HOLDING THE RESERVE
phases.lead: Hold the enemy battalion's attention and force on you until the main attack goes in at its set time.

protocol.Go signal: The codeword FALSE WEIGHT, sent twice, means the main attack has gone in and you may pull out.
protocol.Backup channel: If the main channel is jammed, one short burst on the backup frequency gives the same order to pull out.

phases.name: BREAK — THE TURNING TIDE
phases.lead: Pull out in the short gap between the main attack going in and the enemy battalion turning to hunt you.

sidebarKernel.kernel: the read on whether the enemy battalion has spotted the real attack yet, and how far forward your company is when it does.

assetDetails.detail: Holds the radio plan and the schedule for the main attack. Warns that jamming means the go signal may come late, garbled, or only on the backup channel.
Must be aggressive enough to convince the enemy, yet strong enough to pull out. The same company that sells the fake attack has to survive the battalion turning on it.

title: OPERATION QUIET QUARTER
skeleton: a security force must hunt a shoot-and-scoot artillery battery that fires from protected sites inside a living residential district, where the clean kill is the brief transit window between nests and the fast kill is the block-leveling shot that loses the very population the defender is protecting and hands the enemy a propaganda victory worth more than the guns
inspiration: the urban counter-battery problem of a city under shoot-and-scoot bombardment, Sarajevo, 1992-1995
situation: The guns fire from inside the homes of the people {EMPLOYER} is paid to protect. That is the whole problem. A {TARGET_FACTION} loyalist artillery unit on {WORLD} is shelling the government quarter of {DISTRICT}. Its guns fire from spots hidden in a working-class neighborhood: a school courtyard one hour, a warehouse dock the next, a market square after that. They fire, then move, and they are gone before your return fire can hit back. They picked these spots on purpose. The only fast way to silence a gun is to level the city block around it, killing civilians and handing the enemy a propaganda win worth more than the guns. Your spotters can find the guns; that part is easy. The guns pack up and move slowly enough that a fast team can sometimes catch a crew in the open between sites. The hard part is that every gun you find is firing from a place you cannot simply blow apart. Each time, your clock is short: it is the few minutes it takes a self-propelled gun (an armored vehicle that carries its own cannon) to pack up and drive to its next hidden spot. The enemy commander is not hiding from you. He wants you to take the block-leveling shot that turns the neighborhood against you, and he is betting your restraint keeps him alive. Over three days your spotters have half-mapped his firing pattern. It is good enough to predict the next general area, but not the exact spot. So you must hunt these guns through a living city and kill the crews without killing the neighborhood. Often the easiest shot is the one you are not allowed to take, because it would kill civilians.

objectives.primary: Find and destroy the {TARGET_FACTION} hit-and-run artillery unit shelling the government quarter. Keep civilian harm low enough that the district stays loyal.
objectives.secondary: Capture a gun or a crew intact. It would reveal the enemy's firing schedule.
objectives.bonus: Capture the unit's command team. That breaks the whole schedule at once, instead of killing the guns one by one.

complications.name: The Protected Nest
complications.text: Every firing spot sits where a clean kill would also kill civilians: a courtyard between apartment blocks, a square ringed by shops. The enemy picked these spots on purpose. The shot that kills a gun fastest is the shot that turns the neighborhood against you.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Attacking a gun at its firing spot risks civilian deaths, which raise district hostility. Holding fire to avoid that is slower and lets crews escape more often.

complications.name: The Limber Clock
complications.text: Once a self-propelled gun stops to fire, it has only minutes before it packs up and drives to its next hidden spot. The clean kill is catching it moving on an open street, where a fight harms no one. But those moving-between-sites windows are short, and you have to be in place when one opens.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each gun has a short window while it is moving when you can attack it with no risk to civilians. Miss that window and you must choose: take the shot at its hidden spot and risk civilians, or let the gun escape.

complications.name: Spotters in the Crowd
complications.text: The enemy has spotters in the neighborhood: observers in plain clothes who correct the guns' aim and watch for your hunting team. You cannot tell them from ordinary residents. A rough house-to-house search for them costs you more loyalty than the shelling does.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Hidden observers warn the guns of your movements, so the guns pack up early when they see you coming. Finding the observers takes patient, low-key methods, or you accept that the guns keep getting warned.

decisionPoints.name: The Rules of the Hunt
decisionPoints.context: The rules you set for attacking the guns shape the whole operation. The fastest method turns the district against you. The cleanest method lets some guns escape.

options.title: Restraint absolute - transit kills only
advantages: No civilian harm, so the district stays loyal
Gives the enemy no propaganda win
Catching guns in the open makes captures and crew kills cleaner
disadvantages: Slow, so many guns escape between their short moving windows
The shelling lasts longer, costing lives in the government quarter
Needs near-perfect positioning to catch guns as they move
options.consequence: You keep the neighborhood on your side. In return, the enemy unit survives longer and kills more before you finish it.

costs.resource: extra days of shelling allowed to continue
costs.risk: the government quarter keeps taking casualties while you hunt clean

options.title: Permit collateral at the nests
advantages: Destroys the enemy unit much faster
Stops the shelling of the government quarter sooner
Wipes out the threat for good before it can scatter
disadvantages: Civilians die in the neighborhood
Hands {TARGET_FACTION} a propaganda win
Turns the working-class neighborhood against {EMPLOYER}
options.consequence: The guns die quickly, and the district's loyalty dies with them. You trade one group of people's safety for another's.

costs.resource: the neighborhood's loyalty, given up
costs.risk: the civilian deaths become the enemy's main recruiting and propaganda tool

options.title: Cordon a sector, force the firing window
advantages: Takes away the enemy's safe firing spots, forcing worse ones or more movement
Focuses your careful, hold-fire tactics where they matter most
Can trap the guns' route on ground you control
disadvantages: Sealing off a residential area is disruptive and resented on its own
Pulls hunters away to man the checkpoints
The enemy may just move its guns to a neighborhood you have not sealed
options.consequence: You limit the enemy's options, but you disrupt the very people you are protecting. You are betting you can trap the guns before they move to fresh ground.

costs.resource: one residential area sealed off
costs.risk: the guns slip past the checkpoints and start firing from a fresh neighborhood you have not mapped

decisionPoints.name: A Gun in the Open
decisionPoints.context: Your hunting team catches a gun in the open, but its escort of two fast vehicles sits between you and a clean shot. If you fire, a stray round could hit the apartment blocks behind it. You have seconds to decide.

options.title: Take the shot through the escort
advantages: Kills the gun before it reaches its next hidden spot
Removes one gun from the schedule for good
Killing it in the open is still cleaner than hitting it at a firing spot
disadvantages: The escort and the angle risk a round hitting the apartment blocks behind
A miss, or a shot that punches through, means civilian deaths you chose to risk
Locks your team into a fast, messy street fight
options.consequence: You probably kill the gun, but you accept a real chance of the civilian harm you have been trying to avoid.

costs.resource: a civilian-harm risk you chose to take
costs.risk: a missed shot, or one that punches through the target, hits the housing behind

options.title: Engage the escort, herd the gun
advantages: Clears the escort first, opening a clean shot or a capture
Keeps your fire pointed away from the housing
May make the gun crew surrender instead of dying
disadvantages: The delay may let the gun reach its next nest
Fighting the escort first risks losing the gun entirely
A longer engagement draws civilian eyes and the battery's observers
options.consequence: You fight clean and may lose the gun because it is faster than you, but the housing stays intact.

costs.resource: time spent clearing the escort
costs.risk: the gun packs up and escapes while you deal with its guards

options.title: Let it go, set the next ambush
advantages: Risks nothing: no civilian harm, no exposure
Uses this sighting to predict the next move and get in position early
Trades this gun for a clean shot at the next window
disadvantages: The gun reaches safety and fires again
Relies on a schedule prediction that is only half-reliable
More shelling of the government quarter in the meantime
options.consequence: You hold your fire and gamble that waiting buys a cleaner kill than this one would have been.

costs.resource: one firing cycle given up
costs.risk: the prediction is wrong and the next clean window never comes

entries.event: The enemy guns open their day's fire on the government quarter from their first hidden spot.
The gun packs up and starts driving to its next firing spot. The first clean window opens and closes.
The enemy's observers spot your hunting team on the move. The guns start packing up and leaving even earlier.
Civilian casualty reports from the government quarter pile up. Pressure builds to end the shelling at any cost.
If you have not trapped him, the enemy commander moves the guns to a fresh neighborhood you have not yet mapped.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Destroy the enemy guns before one of two things happens: the shelling breaks the government quarter's will, or the pressure forces you to take the block-leveling shot that hands {TARGET_FACTION} its win.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} hit-and-run artillery unit: 3-4 self-propelled guns (tracked, lightly armored, quick to pack up) plus a screen of fast escort vehicles - hover or wheeled SRM/autocannon carriers (vehicleShare carries guns and escorts; this fight is mostly vehicles and the few 'Mechs that hunt them). A light 'Mech lance, Regular quality, guards the guns and counterattacks any hunting team that pins a gun down. The unit never stands and fights: it fires, packs up, and runs, breaking off the moment its escape is threatened. Observers in plain clothes are part of the story, not on-table units.
opforSketch.behavior: Pure hit-and-run survival that turns the player's restraint into a weapon. The guns fire from spots ringed by civilians, move before return fire lands, and use the crowded streets as cover. The covering 'Mech lance exists to make the hunt costly and to pull out any gun caught in the open.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN SILENCE
forks.trigger: The battery is destroyed with civilian harm kept low and the government quarter's loyalty intact.
forks.consequence: The shelling ends and the district holds for {EMPLOYER}; the next task is hunting the observer network the battery left behind before another battery uses it.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN ROTATION
forks.trigger: The battery's command element is taken, breaking the rotation outright and yielding its firing-plan intelligence.
forks.consequence: The whole battery collapses at once and the captured plans expose the enemy's counter-fire doctrine; {EMPLOYER} turns the intelligence against the next loyalist battery.

forks.name: OPERATION ASHEN QUARTER
forks.trigger: Collateral damage turns the residential quarter hostile, or the battery escapes intact to a fresh district.
forks.consequence: The district's loyalty fractures and the shelling continues from new ground; what was a security operation becomes a counter-insurgency in a quarter that now shelters the guns.

storyElementSeed: A 'Mech holds its fire on a self-propelled gun rolling between two apartment blocks. The gunner watches laundry sway on a line strung across the street, and the few seconds it would take to pack up and escape slip away.

phases.name: MAPPING — THE ROTATION
phases.lead: Build the enemy's firing pattern from your spotters' reports, then set the rules you will hunt under.

dataBlock.Artillery unit: 3-4 self-propelled guns, quick to pack up and move
dataBlock.Moving window per gun: a few minutes - your only clean shot
dataBlock.Schedule intel: next area predictable, exact spot not

sidebarKernel.kernel: how reliable the half-built firing pattern is, and whether the enemy's observers have your hunting team in sight.

phases.name: HUNT — THE LIVING CITY
phases.lead: Work the short moving windows and the hidden firing spots. Kill guns cleanly where you can, and refuse the shot that turns the neighborhood against you where you cannot.

routes.name: TRANSIT LANES
routes.desc: The streets the guns use to move between firing spots.
routes.tradeoff: This is your clean killing ground, but the windows are short and timing is everything.

routes.name: OVERWATCH
routes.desc: Rooftop and tower positions that watch over several firing spots at once.
routes.tradeoff: Sees the most, but a team parked on overwatch is not out chasing the moving guns.

protocol.Spotter call: Spotters report a gun on the move using a location code, and the hunting team races the clock before it packs up.
protocol.Hold-fire order: The codeword QUIET QUARTER means no shot that risks the housing - take the gun cleanly or let it run.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — ENDING IT
phases.lead: Destroy the enemy unit before the shelling, or the pressure over civilian deaths, forces a choice that costs you the district either way.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether to keep killing the guns cleanly one by one, or gamble on trapping the command team and ending it all at once.

assetDetails.detail: Runs the spotter network. Can predict the enemy's next general area, but warns that the exact firing spot is always a guess until the first round lands.
Living under the shelling and counting on you for protection. Every day the enemy guns survive costs lives here, and that is the pressure the enemy is using against you.

title: OPERATION OVERNIGHT BORDER
skeleton: a stranded foreign company must self-extract overland through a region whose garrison switched allegiance overnight, paced by its own wounded and a hard fuel floor it cannot refill on the hostile side, against a pursuit that knows its doctrine and faces because the hunters were its allies the day before, where the enemy's own post-flip confusion is the only thing keeping the net loose enough to slip
inspiration: the fighting overland withdrawal of a force suddenly behind enemy lines - the Anabasis march of the Ten Thousand, 401 BC
situation: The garrison command on {WORLD} switched sides overnight. Your company is a hired merc force on a quiet rotation deep in {DISTRICT}. When you went to sleep this was friendly ground. When you woke it was enemy ground, held by the same people you shared a mess with the day before. {EMPLOYER}'s nearest line is about four days away on foot and tracks. Every checkpoint and fuel depot between here and there changed hands at once. Your paymaster is now on the far side of a war you did not start, and the new commander wants to capture your company intact. He would either turn it to his side or execute it as a warning. You have your 'Mechs, your support vehicles, your wounded, and only so much fuel. There are no friendly depots on this side to refuel from, so once the fuel runs out, machines have to be abandoned. The enemy is organizing a pursuit, but he is also busy with his own mess: some of his units did not switch sides, and his command is improvising as it goes. That confusion is the only thing keeping his net loose enough to slip through. Your task is to march the company home. Fight only when you must, avoid it when you can, and decide at each step how much of the column you will risk to save the rest. This is not a battle to win. It is a retreat to survive.

objectives.primary: March the whole company out of the flipped {DISTRICT} to {EMPLOYER}'s nearest line, about four days away. Bring the 'Mechs, the support vehicles, and the wounded.
objectives.secondary: Arrive with the support vehicles and wounded, not just the 'Mechs.
objectives.bonus: Escape without losing a single 'Mech to the pursuit. This keeps the company's full fighting strength and its reputation.

complications.name: Yesterday's Allies
complications.text: The garrison hunting you knows how you fight, what your machines can do, and the faces of your officers. Last week you shared a mess with them. They can predict any routine you have used before. Assume everything they knew about you is still true.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The enemy predicts your normal movement and rest patterns. If you behave predictably, the column walks into a prepared ambush.

complications.name: The Fuel Floor
complications.text: You have a fixed amount of fuel, and the depots you would have used now belong to the enemy. You cannot refuel on this side of the line. Every detour to dodge a fight, and every fast run to break away, spends fuel you cannot get back.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Fuel is a hard limit. Fast evasion and long detours burn it quickly. Run out and 'Mechs or vehicles get stranded and abandoned before they reach the line.

complications.name: The Slowest Wagon
complications.text: The wounded and the repair vehicles set the column's real speed. The 'Mechs could move fast on their own, but the column cannot. Protecting these slow elements is the hard part, and every fight makes leaving them behind more tempting.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The wounded and support vehicles cap the whole column's speed. Leaving them behind speeds up the 'Mechs but loses the secondary objective and the people in that train.

decisionPoints.name: The Route Home
decisionPoints.context: Three routes lead to the line. The highway is fast but watched. The back country is slow and burns a lot of fuel. The river valley is in between, but its crossings are dangerous.

options.title: The highway - fast and seen
advantages: Fastest route, uses the least fuel
Easy going for the support vehicles
Reaches the line before the pursuit is fully organized
disadvantages: This is the obvious route, so the enemy blocks it first
No cover if a blocking force sets up ahead of you
Every switched checkpoint sits right on it
options.consequence: You move fast and bet you can beat the enemy to the road he knows you would take.

costs.resource: Uses the least fuel, but leaves you the most exposed
costs.risk: A blocking force set up on the highway pins the column in the open

options.title: The back country - slow and thirsty
advantages: Avoids the watched routes and the switched checkpoints
The hardest ground for the enemy to block or reach
Gives the enemy's confusion more time to work in your favor
disadvantages: Burns the most fuel, over the worst terrain
The slowest route, and the wounded suffer for it
A breakdown out here can strand a vehicle for good
options.consequence: You vanish into rough country and race your fuel gauge to the line.

costs.resource: Burns the most fuel and is the slowest route
costs.risk: You run out of fuel before reaching the line and must abandon 'Mechs

options.title: The river valley - the middle road
advantages: The river and its tree lines hide the column from the air
Reasonable going for the support vehicles
Narrow spots let a rearguard hold and delay pursuers
disadvantages: River crossings are perfect spots for an ambush or a block
A column pinned against the water cannot move or spread out
The enemy knows the valley's narrow points as well as you do
options.consequence: You take the middle route, and the crossings decide whether you make it.

costs.resource: Moderate fuel, but the crossings are the danger
costs.risk: A blown or blocked crossing traps the column against the river

decisionPoints.name: Contact at the Crossing
decisionPoints.context: An enemy armor company has set up a roadblock at a narrow point on your route. You can fight through it, go around it, or try to buy it off. Because you are mercenaries, buying passage is an option a regular unit would not have.

options.title: Force the block
advantages: Clears the route for good
A beaten roadblock force cannot chase you
Keeps the column moving on the route you chose
disadvantages: A stand-up fight burns fuel, ammo, and machines you cannot replace
Wounded you then have to carry the rest of the march
Noise and wreckage that mark your position for the pursuit
options.consequence: You break through, but you spend the fuel and ammo that were meant to get you home.

costs.resource: Fuel and ammo spent in a stand-up fight
costs.risk: A hard fight here leaves the company too weak to survive the next one

options.title: Slip around it
advantages: Avoids the fight and keeps your fighting strength
Saves your fuel for the distance instead of the battle
Denies the enemy the fight he set up
disadvantages: The detour costs time and fuel and strains the support vehicles
Going around leaves the roadblock force free to follow you
The ground around the roadblock may be worse than the roadblock
options.consequence: You go around, trading extra distance and fuel to keep the company whole.

costs.resource: Extra fuel for the detour and a day's time
costs.risk: The detour strands a vehicle, or the roadblock force catches your tail

options.title: Talk your way through - you are mercenaries
advantages: Some of the enemy switched sides under orders, not by choice, and may let fellow professionals pass
Costs no fuel, ammo, or machines if it works
Opens contact that may ease the rest of the march
disadvantages: The talks could be a trap to hold you in place while heavier forces arrive
If it fails, you have shown the enemy your position, strength, and plan
The new command may have already made an example of fence-sitters
options.consequence: You bet that professional respect outlasts the coup, and find out whether the men across the line still treat you as colleagues.

costs.resource: A bribe or a favor owed, if the talks work
costs.risk: The talks are a trap and a heavier force closes in while you speak

entries.event: The switch is confirmed. The company is now a foreign unit on hostile ground, and the march begins.
The enemy garrison sorts out its own confusion and turns real attention to the merc company behind it.
Roadblocks appear on the obvious routes. The enemy starts steering where you can go.
Fuel runs low. Your choices narrow to the routes you can still afford to take.
You approach {EMPLOYER}'s line. Here the enemy makes his last and hardest try to capture the company before it crosses.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Reach {EMPLOYER}'s line before the fuel runs out or the pursuit pins you down. A merc company captured intact is a prize the new command will not let go.

opforSketch.composition: The enemy garrison's pursuit, thrown together and growing. It starts with a mixed chase company: 8-12 medium 'Mechs (40-65 tons, Regular) and a slice of fast combat vehicles for the roadblocks and scouting (vehicleShare carries the blockers and scouts). As the garrison gets organized, armor companies set up roadblocks on the routes ahead. Its own post-switch disorder keeps it from committing everything at once. The roadblocks aim to pin and delay you, not to win outright. The enemy is betting your fuel and his closing net will do the real work.
opforSketch.behavior: Block and delay. Cut the obvious routes, push the column toward ground the enemy has prepared, and use his close knowledge of how the merc unit fights. His own confusion is the only thing keeping his net loose enough to slip through.

forks.name: OPERATION HOME LINE
forks.trigger: The company reaches {EMPLOYER}'s line with its 'Mechs and most of the column intact.
forks.consequence: The company crosses to friendly ground and reconstitutes; {EMPLOYER} folds it into the new line, its contract and reputation intact.

forks.name: OPERATION WHOLE COLUMN
forks.trigger: The company exits without losing a 'Mech and brings every wounded crew and support vehicle out.
forks.consequence: A clean withdrawal that costs the company nothing and embarrasses the flipped garrison; the unit's reputation for getting its people out becomes a recruiting and contract asset.

forks.name: OPERATION CUT OFF
forks.trigger: Fuel runs out or the pursuit pins the column short of the line.
forks.consequence: The company is fixed in hostile territory and fights to break out on foot and in fragments; what gets home is a remnant, and the rest is captured or destroyed.

storyElementSeed: By a shielded lamp, the company quartermaster checks the fuel gauge against the map. She works out how far the fuel will take them, the way she has at every halt, and likes the answer no better this time.

phases.name: WAKE — THE GROUND THAT TURNED
phases.lead: Confirm the switch, count your fuel and wounded, and choose the route home before the enemy garrison gets organized.

dataBlock.Distance to line: about 4 days on foot and tracks
dataBlock.Fuel reserve: fixed amount; no friendly depots on this side
dataBlock.Column: 'Mechs, support vehicles, wounded - moves at the speed of the slowest
dataBlock.Pursuit: the enemy garrison, getting organized as it goes

sidebarKernel.kernel: how many days of fuel are left for each route, and which vehicles will run dry first.

phases.name: MARCH — THROUGH HOSTILE COUNTRY
phases.lead: Move toward the line through ground that switched sides overnight. Fight only when you must, and never in a way the enemy can predict.

routes.name: HIGHWAY
routes.desc: The fast, watched main road.
routes.tradeoff: Quickest and uses the least fuel, but blocked first and exposed the whole way.

routes.name: BACK COUNTRY
routes.desc: The rough route around the checkpoints.
routes.tradeoff: Hardest for the enemy to block, but burns the most fuel and is worst for the wounded.

routes.name: RIVER VALLEY
routes.desc: The hidden middle road along the river.
routes.tradeoff: Covered and passable, but the crossings are the enemy's chosen ambush ground.

protocol.Halt discipline: Never stop the same way twice. The enemy knows the company's old habits.
protocol.Contact code: Codeword OVERNIGHT BORDER switches the column to the rearguard plan when it hits a roadblock.

phases.name: CROSSING — THE HOME LINE
phases.lead: Make the final push to {EMPLOYER}'s line while the enemy makes his last and hardest try to capture the company before it crosses.

sidebarKernel.kernel: what fuel, machines, and crews the company can still spend to get the rest across the line.

assetDetails.detail: Sets the column's real speed and cannot defend itself. The hard part of the march is refusing to leave it behind.
