A hard limit that every detour and every sprint draws down, with no resupply until the line. Fuel decides the route as much as the enemy does.

title: OPERATION OPEN PALM
skeleton: a defender must run an elastic defense-in-depth, yielding pre-built forward belts on cue to channel a heavier armored thrust into a pre-ranged killing zone, where the discipline of selling each loss as real is the whole plan - springing the trap too early catches only the vanguard and too late lets a belt be overrun and the channeling collapse behind the prepared ground
inspiration: the elastic box-and-killing-ground defense of the Gazala cauldron, 1942
situation: The way to beat a heavier attacker is to let him in, and letting him in is the hard part. {TARGET_FACTION} is driving an armored thrust into {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}. It is a reinforced battalion of heavy 'Mechs and tracked armor, aimed at {EMPLOYER}'s supply hub, and it is too strong to stop head-on. So you do not try to stop it head-on. {EMPLOYER}'s engineers have spent two weeks building a layered defense. Up front are positions you plan to give up. Behind them are minefields and obstacles set not to block the enemy but to funnel him. Beyond that is a killing zone in the low ground, where your guns are already aimed and ranged. Once the enemy is funneled and stretched out there, you can cut him apart on ground you chose. Your company holds the forward positions, and your discipline is the whole plan. You must fight hard enough at each one that the enemy thinks he is breaking your main line. Then you give it up on signal and fall back to the next, drawing him deeper and letting him think he is winning, right up until he is standing in the open ground built to kill him. Pull back too early and he senses the trap, gets cautious, and refuses the bait. Hold too long and he overruns a position and breaks through your whole depth before the trap can spring. You know his likely line of advance, because the terrain funnels him. What you cannot know in advance is his exact timing, or whether he will send in his reserve to exploit what looks like a breakthrough. That is a call you make in the moment. Open your hand to draw him in, then close it into a fist. Close too soon and you catch nothing.

objectives.primary: Funnel the {TARGET_FACTION} armored thrust into the prepared killing zone and destroy or break it there, holding {EMPLOYER}'s supply hub.
objectives.secondary: Keep the forward-position force alive through the planned pullbacks. Give up the ground without losing the units that hold it.
objectives.bonus: Draw the enemy's follow-up reserve into the killing zone too, so the whole thrust is broken beyond recovery.

complications.name: The Discipline of Retreat
complications.text: You must fight for each forward position in a way that looks real, then give it up on time. Hold one a moment too long and it gets overrun. Give one up too easily and the enemy realizes you meant to lose it. The trap works only if every loss looks genuine.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each planned pullback has a timing window. Pull back too late and that position's force gets pinned and destroyed. Pull back too early and the enemy grows cautious and may stop short of the killing zone.

complications.name: The Cautious Enemy
complications.text: A good attacker scouts before he commits and stops if the ground feels wrong. If your funneling is too obvious, or your pullbacks look too neat, he halts at the edge of the killing zone and refuses to enter it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Whether the enemy enters the killing zone depends on how convincing the forward fight was. A weak fight leaves him short of the trap, and then you must lure him forward at greater risk.

complications.name: The Overrun Belt
complications.text: If a forward position breaks before you signal the pullback, the funnel collapses. The enemy pours through on his own terms, behind your prepared ground instead of into it. Your layered defense turns into a string of cut-off positions instead of a trap.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A position lost out of order lets the enemy break through where you did not plan. The killing zone's pre-aimed fire no longer lines up, and the defense falls apart.

decisionPoints.name: The Depth of the Bait
decisionPoints.context: How far you let the enemy come before you spring the trap decides everything. Spring early and you catch part of him, but on safer terms. Spring late and you can catch all of him, but at greater risk.

options.title: Spring early, catch the vanguard
advantages: Less chance a position is overrun before the trap closes
Catches the enemy's lead group cleanly
Keeps more of the forward-position force alive
disadvantages: The enemy's main weight is still outside the killing zone
A battered lead group warns the units behind it
A partial win that leaves the thrust able to regroup
options.consequence: You hit the lead group on good terms and let the rest of the thrust stop short and survive.

costs.resource: Only part of the killing zone gets used
costs.risk: The enemy's main body halts outside the trap and comes on again on its own terms

options.title: Spring deep, catch the battalion
advantages: Draws the enemy's full weight onto ground where your guns are already aimed and ranged
The decisive result: it breaks the thrust outright
Puts two weeks of engineering to full use in one fight
disadvantages: You must hold the forward positions to the last safe moment
Highest risk that a position is overrun before the trap closes
Spring it wrong and you catch nothing and leave your whole depth exposed
options.consequence: You hold your nerve to the edge of disaster. You either break the whole battalion or get overrun trying.

costs.resource: forward-position risk is at its highest
costs.risk: a forward position breaks early and the funnel collapses before the trap springs

options.title: Bait the reserve too
advantages: Fakes a real breakthrough to pull the follow-up reserve in behind the lead group
Catches the entire thrust, reserve included, in one trap
The most complete victory you can get
disadvantages: You must stage a convincing collapse, which is one step from a real one
The deepest, riskiest use of the forward force
If the fake collapse turns real, the hub is lost
options.consequence: You dangle a fake breakthrough and bet the enemy's greed pulls his reserve into the fire with the rest.

costs.resource: a fake collapse staged at real risk
costs.risk: the staged collapse turns real and the enemy pours through a breach you cannot close

decisionPoints.name: The Reserve Commitment
decisionPoints.context: Your held-back reserve is the force that closes the trap, and it must commit at exactly the right moment. Hold it too long and the enemy may escape the killing zone. Spend it too early and you have nothing left for a second push.

options.title: Commit on the enemy's lead reaching the mark
advantages: Closes the trap at the by-the-book moment
Catches the funneled force when it is stretched out and thin
Leaves some room to spare if you have judged the ground right
disadvantages: If the enemy's main body lags behind, you spring on the lead group alone
You commit the reserve before the full picture is clear
Misjudge where the lead group is and the trap closes on empty ground
options.consequence: You trust the plan and close the trap the moment the lead group hits its mark, for better or worse.

costs.resource: the reserve is committed on the lead group
costs.risk: the main body has not entered yet and the trap catches only the lead group

options.title: Hold until the enemy is fully committed
advantages: Makes sure the most enemy weight possible is inside the killing zone
The reserve hits a force that can no longer pull back
Decisive if your timing holds
disadvantages: Holding the reserve longer means the forward positions take more punishment
The enemy may start to sense the trap before you spring it
Commit too late and the reserve arrives after the best moment has passed
options.consequence: You wait until the whole enemy force is inside, and risk your forward positions breaking before you spring.

costs.resource: the forward positions take losses while the reserve waits
costs.risk: the enemy reads the trap and starts pulling back before the reserve commits

options.title: Split the reserve, close in two stages
advantages: The first commitment pins the enemy, the second finishes him
Protects you if you misjudge his timing
Keeps a force in hand as a follow-up reserve
disadvantages: A split reserve hits with less weight at each stage
Two commitments mean two chances to get the timing wrong
Neither stage may be strong enough to decide the fight on its own
options.consequence: You close the trap in two stages, trading the power of one big blow for a safety net against mistiming.

costs.resource: reserve weight split across two commitments
costs.risk: neither half is strong enough to break the enemy and he fights his way clear

entries.event: The {TARGET_FACTION} armored thrust enters the district and hits the first forward position.
You make the first planned pullback. The enemy takes the position and reads it as a breakthrough or a trap.
The thrust is funneled into the obstacle lanes and stretches out along the path the terrain forces on it.
The enemy's lead group nears the killing zone. Now you must choose: spring early, or hold for the main body.
The enemy either sends in his follow-up reserve or holds it back, depending on whether he believes the breakthrough is real.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Spring the trap before a forward position is overrun out of order. Once the funnel collapses, the enemy is loose behind your prepared ground and the supply hub is open.

opforSketch.composition: A reinforced {TARGET_FACTION} armored battalion: 24-30 heavy and medium 'Mechs (50-80 tons, Regular with a Veteran spearhead) plus a strong tracked-armor force of heavy tanks and assault vehicles to add weight to the thrust (vehicleShare carries the armor that makes this a combined-arms drive). The thrust pushes hard down the funnel but scouts before it enters risky ground. It keeps a follow-up reserve ready to pour through any breakthrough it sees. It sends the reserve in when it believes it has broken through, and turns cautious if it senses a trap.
opforSketch.behavior: An aggressive armored drive at the supply hub, run by professionals careful enough to fear an obvious trap. Its strength is its weight, and its weakness is its hunger for a breakthrough. Your defense uses both against it.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED FIST
forks.trigger: The thrust is channeled into the killing zone and broken; the logistics hub holds.
forks.consequence: The enemy battalion is shattered in the prepared ground and {EMPLOYER}'s hub is secure; the freed defense can counterattack the thrust's broken remnants.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY HAND
forks.trigger: The enemy's exploitation reserve is drawn in and destroyed with the lead, breaking the thrust beyond recovery.
forks.consequence: The entire thrust, reserve included, is annihilated in the killing zone; the enemy's offensive capability in the sector collapses and {EMPLOYER} can go over to the attack.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN HAND
forks.trigger: A forward belt is overrun out of sequence or the trap springs on empty ground.
forks.consequence: The channeling collapses and the enemy breaks through behind the prepared depth; the defense fragments into isolated positions fighting to cover the now-exposed logistics hub.

storyElementSeed: A position commander orders his crews to abandon ground they bled to hold an hour ago. He watches the enemy roll onto it and call it a win. He knows that win is the bait.

phases.name: POSTURE — THE BELTS AND THE GROUND
phases.lead: Set the forward positions, check that the obstacle lanes and pre-aimed guns are ready, and brief the crews on the discipline the trap depends on.

dataBlock.Forward belts: 3 positions, each fought hard then given up on signal
dataBlock.Obstacle lanes: minefields and barriers set to steer the enemy, not stop him
dataBlock.Killing zone: low ground past the last position, guns already aimed and ranged
dataBlock.Husbanded reserve: the force held back to close the trap

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the obstacle lanes are funneling the enemy as planned, and which positions can hold to their signal versus which are giving way too soon.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — DRAWING HIM IN
phases.lead: Fight for each position so the enemy believes it, then give it up on time, drawing the thrust deeper toward the ground you prepared.

routes.name: OBSTACLE LANES
routes.desc: The paths between the minefields that steer the enemy's advance.
routes.tradeoff: They funnel the enemy where you want him, but fight too hard for a lane and he sees it was a funnel.

routes.name: FALLBACK ROUTES
routes.desc: The covered paths the crews use to pull back between positions.
routes.tradeoff: They let a position's force pull back cleanly, but a pullback that looks too neat tips off the trap.

protocol.Withdrawal cue: Codeword OPEN PALM releases a position. The force holding it gives it up and falls back on its route.
protocol.Spring signal: Codeword CLOSED FIST sends in the reserve, and the killing zone opens fire.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE FIST CLOSES
phases.lead: Spring the trap once the enemy is deep enough, and send in the reserve to break the thrust in the killing zone.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether enough of the enemy is deep enough to spring the trap, and whether his reserve has taken the bait or is holding back.

assetDetails.detail: Asked to fight hard and lose on schedule, three times. These crews give up ground they bled for, and that discipline is what the whole plan rests on.
The force that closes the trap. Spend it too early and it catches only the lead group. Hold it too long and it arrives after the best moment. You must commit it on a read made in seconds.

title: OPERATION GLASS HALL
skeleton: a 'Mech force must neutralize a hostage-barricade's dug-in heavy weapons and seal its exits to enable an inside assault force to retake the building, unable to fire on a structure packed with hostages where the enemy's heaviest machine shelters in the atrium, racing a named hostage-execution clock and a hostage-shielded breakout threat at once
inspiration: the barricade-hostage assault of the Iranian Embassy siege, Operation Nimrod, 1980
situation: A splinter command has barricaded itself inside a government complex on {WORLD} with several dozen civilian hostages. It is using those hostages as human shields. The unit declared for {TARGET_FACTION}. It was cut off when the surrounding district stayed loyal. Instead of surrendering, it seized the regional government hall in {DISTRICT} and packed it with hostages. The hall holds offices, a public atrium, and a parking garage. The hostages are office workers, visitors, and families pulled off the street. Their demands change every hour. Their commander has nothing left to lose, and he has promised to kill hostages. {EMPLOYER} has surrounded the complex. A 'Mech cannot end a hostage siege by firepower alone. The splinter command chose this building because it knew you would not destroy it with hostages inside. An assault force of infantry and specialists will retake the hall from inside. They cannot go in until the barricade's heavy weapons are dealt with and its exits are sealed. That is your company's job. Kill or suppress the 'Mechs and combat vehicles dug in around the complex. Seal the parking garage and the service roads so no one can break out. Do all of this without collapsing the building or setting off the massacre the assault is meant to stop. You know where the hostages are only as a rough, floor-by-floor guess. That guess comes from a few smuggled phone calls and one civilian who escaped through a window. The barricade has set its own deadline. The commander has named an hour when he will start killing hostages. Everyone is racing that clock.

objectives.primary: Destroy or suppress the splinter command's 'Mechs and combat vehicles, then seal the complex so no one escapes. This lets the assault force retake the hall before the commander's deadline.
objectives.secondary: Stop any part of the barricade from escaping into the district with hostages.
objectives.bonus: Suppress the heavy weapons so well that the enemy is already breaking when the assault goes in. This saves the most hostages.

complications.name: The Building You Cannot Break
complications.text: The hostages are inside a building your weapons could collapse. Any shot near the hall could kill the people you are trying to save. The enemy knows this. Their heaviest 'Mech sits in the atrium, where you cannot fire on it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Firing on enemy units inside or against the hall can collapse the building and kill hostages. You can only handle those units by luring them out or leaving them to the assault force.

complications.name: The Breakout Threat
complications.text: A cornered force may try to run. It would use hostages as a moving shield and push out through the parking garage or the service roads. If it reaches the district, a contained crisis becomes a hostage chase across the city.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If you press the barricade before its exits are sealed, it tries to break out with hostages. Any exit you leave open lets a hostage-shielded group escape into the district.

complications.name: The Commander's Clock
complications.text: The commander has named an hour when he will begin killing hostages. He has already kept smaller threats to prove he means this one. You cannot wait him out. This deadline drives the whole operation.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A hard execution deadline runs the whole mission. Miss an intermediate deadline and the commander kills hostages and grows more stubborn. Each miss removes a gentler way to end the crisis.

decisionPoints.name: How to Set the Stage for the Assault
decisionPoints.context: The assault force cannot move until you handle the barricade's heavy weapons and exits. How you handle them decides the assault's odds and the hostages' chances.

options.title: Draw the heavy 'Mechs out
advantages: Pulls the dug-in 'Mechs away from the hall, where you can safely fight them
Clears the building of the weapons you could not fire on before
Leaves the assault force a building with no enemy armor inside
disadvantages: If the trick fails, the 'Mechs stay put and now know your plan
Drawing them out may trigger the breakout you are trying to prevent
It takes time, and the hostage clock may not allow it
options.consequence: If the bait works, the assault goes in clean. If it fails, you have shown your plan and wasted time.

costs.resource: time spent luring the armor out
costs.risk: the lure triggers a breakout, or fails and warns the barricade

options.title: Seal everything, starve them out short
advantages: Locks every exit so no breakout is possible
Gives the assault force a fully sealed target
Gives you the tightest control of the perimeter
disadvantages: A tight seal pushes the commander toward his deadline
Leaves the heavy 'Mechs in the hall for the assault to face
A commander with no way out is more likely to start killing
options.consequence: You guarantee that no one escapes, but the pressure may push the commander to start shooting.

costs.resource: perimeter forces tied up holding the seal
costs.risk: the tight seal provokes early hostage killings

options.title: Suppress and overwatch, let the assault dictate
advantages: Keeps the heavy weapons pinned without destroying the building
Lets the assault specialists pick the moment to move
Stays flexible and adapts as the assault unfolds
disadvantages: Pinning a 'Mech is not killing it, so it can still act
Demands tight timing with the assault force under a hard clock
One lapse in fire at the wrong second can get hostages killed
options.consequence: You hold the enemy down and trust the assault to move at the right moment. It works only if your timing is good enough.

costs.resource: constant suppressing fire and coordination
costs.risk: a gap in your fire frees a heavy weapon during the assault

decisionPoints.name: The Breakout Attempt
decisionPoints.context: The barricade tries to run. A group of vehicles and a 'Mech burst from the parking garage with hostages aboard, heading for the service road and the district beyond. You have seconds to react.

options.title: Block the road, force the standoff
advantages: Stops the breakout before it reaches the district
Keeps the crisis in one place where the assault can still end it
Prevents a hostage chase across the city
disadvantages: A hard block risks a firefight with hostages aboard the vehicles
A cornered breakout may fight to the death on the road
Most hostages die when the two forces collide
options.consequence: You stop the breakout, but you accept a close-range fight with hostages caught in the middle.

costs.resource: a forced standoff with hostages present
costs.risk: the blocked breakout fights through and hostages are hit

options.title: Let it run, shadow and channel it
advantages: Avoids an immediate firefight at the exit
Lets the breakout commit to a route you can steer
Opens a chance to intercept it cleanly, away from the hall
disadvantages: A breakout loose in the district is far harder to stop
You may lose it in the maze of city streets
Trades a crisis you have contained for one that is now moving
options.consequence: You let them out and try to steer them to ground you choose. You are betting you can pin them before they vanish.

costs.resource: you give up containment for a cleaner intercept
costs.risk: the breakout escapes into the city and the hostage crisis becomes mobile

options.title: Take the disabling shot
advantages: A precise shot that disables the lead vehicle ends the breakout at once
Stops the run without a long fight
The best outcome of all, if the shot is clean
disadvantages: A shot this close to hostages leaves no margin for error
A miss, or an explosion, kills the people aboard
One shot decides everything, and there is no second try
options.consequence: You bet the hostages' lives on one precise shot and live with the result.

costs.resource: one precise shot, no margin for error
costs.risk: the shot goes wrong and the hostages aboard die

entries.event: The cordon is set. The commander issues his shifting demands and names an hour he will start killing hostages.
You have located the barricade's heavy 'Mechs and vehicles and mapped what each can hit.
The first intermediate deadline passes. The commander harms a hostage to prove the clock is real.
The assault force reports it is ready. It only needs the heavy weapons handled and the exits sealed.
The barricade feels the cordon tightening. It prepares either to make a last stand or to break out with hostages.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Clear the way for the assault before the commander's execution hour. After that hour he starts killing hostages in numbers, and the mission becomes a body recovery instead of a rescue.

opforSketch.composition: A cut-off splinter command, company strength and desperate: 6-9 'Mechs of mixed weight (30-65 tons, Regular, dug in around and inside the complex) and a combat-vehicle slice of armor and transports positioned to cover the exits and mount a breakout (vehicleShare carries the blockers and the breakout vehicles). The heaviest 'Mech is parked inside the atrium, where you cannot fire on it without hitting hostages. The force cannot maneuver freely because it is tied to the hostages. It will fight to the death if cornered, and it will try a hostage-shielded breakout if pressed. Its infantry guard the hostages and do not fight as units on the table.
opforSketch.behavior: A trapped force using the hostages and the building as weapons. It cannot win and knows it. Its only leverage is the threat to the civilians and the building. It fights to force a deal, to break out, or, if denied both, to make the retaking as bloody as it can.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR HALL
forks.trigger: The heavy weapons are neutralized, the exits held, and the assault retakes the hall before the deadline with most hostages alive.
forks.consequence: The barricade is broken and the hall recovered; {EMPLOYER} holds the district's seat of government and the surviving splinter personnel face the consequences of the coup.

forks.name: OPERATION WHOLE GLASS
forks.trigger: The heavy weapons are so cleanly suppressed that the assault goes in against a half-collapsed enemy and the hostages come out nearly whole.
forks.consequence: A near-bloodless resolution that becomes a propaganda and morale victory for {EMPLOYER}; the splinter command's collapse demoralizes other wavering loyalist holdouts in the region.

forks.name: OPERATION SHATTERED HALL
forks.trigger: The deadline passes, a breakout reaches the district, or the building is brought down trying to force a resolution.
forks.consequence: The hostage crisis ends in slaughter or goes mobile across the city; the operation becomes a hunt for a hostage-holding remnant loose in the district, with the political damage already done.

storyElementSeed: An assault-team leader presses against a wall outside the atrium. He listens to the heavy 'Mech idling inside among hostages he cannot see. He waits for word that the 'Mech has been drawn away.

phases.name: CORDON — THE BARRICADE
phases.lead: Set the perimeter, map the barricade's heavy weapons and exits, and gauge how much time is left on the commander's clock.

dataBlock.Hostages: several dozen; locations known only as a floor-by-floor guess
dataBlock.Execution deadline: an hour the commander has named and already shown he means

sidebarKernel.kernel: what the few hostage messages tell you about where the hostages are and what the commander is thinking, and how much you can trust any of it.

phases.name: PREPARE — SETTING THE STAGE
phases.lead: Handle the heavy weapons and seal the exits so the assault force can move. Do it without collapsing the hall or setting off a massacre.

routes.name: SERVICE ROADS
routes.desc: The complex's rear access and loading roads.
routes.tradeoff: The most likely breakout path. Sealing it tight traps the enemy but pushes the commander toward his deadline.

routes.name: PARKING STRUCTURE
routes.desc: The vehicle deck attached to the hall.
routes.tradeoff: Where the breakout vehicles are staged. Controlling it stops the run, but it means close-range fighting near hostages.

protocol.Assault ready-call: The codeword GLASS HALL from the assault force means it will move the instant the heavy weapons are handled.
protocol.Hold signal: The codeword STILL AIR stops all firing, so you do not provoke the commander while negotiators are talking.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE RETAKING
phases.lead: Support the assault as it goes in, or stop the breakout if the barricade runs. Either way, you are racing the execution hour.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the assault has its moment or the barricade is breaking out, and what you can do in the few seconds you have.

assetDetails.detail: Scattered through the complex, their exact spots only a guess. Where they are decides which enemy positions you can fire on and which you cannot. The commander's clock is counting down against their lives.
Handles the close-quarters work inside the hall that 'Mechs cannot. It cannot move until the heavy weapons are dealt with and the exits sealed. Its survival depends on your company's timing.

title: OPERATION WINTER GULLET
skeleton: a company must defeat a road-bound relief column in detail by ambushing and isolating its strung-out march-serials before the column can close up and concentrate into a force that would beat it, weaponizing terrain blocks that are also its own withdrawal hazard, racing the window before the battalion learns it is being eaten and starts fighting as a whole
inspiration: the motti tactics that cut a road-bound column to pieces at Suomussalmi, 1939-1940
situation: A {TARGET_FACTION} relief column is stretched out along forty kilometers of one mountain road. {EMPLOYER} wants you to destroy it piece by piece before it can gather together. The column is a full battalion: 'Mechs, tracked supply trucks, and the families of a loyalist garrison. It is moving to reinforce a position your side plans to take in {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}, and this road is the only way through the high country. If that battalion fought as one, it would beat your company. But the road will not let it gather. The terrain breaks it into small groups strung out far apart. They are split up by hairpin turns, by narrow passes, and by how slowly tracked vehicles climb. Your job is to destroy those groups one at a time. Ambush the lead group, then drop obstacles to cut off the others. That way the column can only ever fight you with a small part of itself, and you beat it piece by piece. The cold and the terrain help you. A stopped group is stuck in place while you work on it. A 'Mech that breaks down in a narrow pass is one the column cannot get moving again. But every ambush warns the column that you are here. A good commander will start pulling his groups closer together and pushing his guards to the threatened spots. The longer you wait, the more the column can fight back as one force. Your intel on how the column is lined up is a day old and incomplete. You know it is coming and roughly how big it is, but not exactly where its combat units sit in the line. Your window is short: it lasts only until the battalion realizes it is under attack and pulls together.

objectives.primary: Destroy or scatter the {TARGET_FACTION} relief column on the mountain road so it cannot reach and reinforce the contested position.
objectives.secondary: Cut off and destroy the column's combat guards one group at a time, before they can pull together into one force.
objectives.bonus: Wreck the column's supply trucks and bridge-building gear so badly that even survivors cannot finish the relief.

complications.name: The Closing Worm
complications.text: Each ambush warns the column. A good commander reacts by pulling his groups closer together and moving guards to the front and rear. He tries to keep any group from being cut off alone. The longer the fight runs, the more the column moves as one solid force.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each fight raises the column's alert level. At higher alert its groups pull together into one force. You can no longer pick them off one at a time, so fights get bigger and more costly.

complications.name: The Frozen Defile
complications.text: A broken-down vehicle or a downed 'Mech in a narrow spot blocks the road for everyone behind it. This can help you or hurt you. A block you set traps an enemy group, but a block in the wrong spot can trap you on the wrong side of it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Obstacles and wrecks close off stretches of road. A block in the right place cuts off an enemy group. A block in the wrong place cuts off your own escape route or your own ambush team.

complications.name: Escorts With Teeth
complications.text: The column's guards are not helpless cargo. They are combat 'Mechs and armored vehicles sent to protect the march. If you ambush a supply group, a lance of guards may reach your ambush team before it can finish and pull out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Combat guards react to an ambush after a short delay. If your ambush team stays in the fight too long, the guards arrive and catch it in the open.

decisionPoints.name: Where to Strike First
decisionPoints.context: Your first ambush shapes how the column reacts. You can hit the front, the rear, or the supply in the middle. Each choice leads to a different fight from there.

options.title: Behead the column
advantages: Stops the whole column from moving forward
A blocked front stops everything behind it
Buys you time to hit the stopped groups
disadvantages: The strongest guards ride at the front
A hard fight against the column's best combat units
Puts the whole column on alert right away
options.consequence: You stop the relief cold, but you pay for it by fighting the column's best-protected units.

costs.resource: a hard fight against the strongest guards at the front
costs.risk: the front guards badly damage your ambush team before the column stops

options.title: Cut the tail
advantages: Cuts off the rear groups with the families and rear supply
Fewer and weaker guards at the rear
Can be done quietly, so the alert spreads slower
disadvantages: The front of the column still reaches its goal
A partial relief still strengthens the contested position
Leaves the column's strongest combat units untouched at the front
options.consequence: You destroy the weak rear but let the strong front get through. The relief is weakened, not stopped.

costs.resource: you let the column's front reach the position
costs.risk: the front arrives undamaged and the relief partly succeeds

options.title: Gut the supply heart
advantages: Destroys the supply and bridge gear that make the relief worth anything
Hits the column where its loss hurts the mission most
A relief that arrives without supply can do little
disadvantages: The supply sits in the middle, the hardest place to reach unseen
Guards from the front and rear close in on an ambush in the center
Requires pushing the deepest into the column, which is the riskiest move
options.consequence: You hit the part that matters most, but you risk being caught between the guards on both sides of it.

costs.resource: a deep ambush with guards on both sides
costs.risk: the front and rear guards close in and trap your ambush team in the middle

decisionPoints.name: When the Column Closes Up
decisionPoints.context: The column's groups are pulling together, so picking them off one by one is no longer easy. You can press harder as the enemy gathers, switch to hit-and-run attacks, or break off with what you have already wrecked.

options.title: Press the concentration
advantages: Keeps the column from finishing its march
Does the most total damage if you can keep it up
Stops the enemy from regrouping and moving on
disadvantages: Fighting the gathered battalion is exactly the fight you wanted to avoid
Your losses climb as the column fights as one force
Risks the enemy picking off your company piece by piece instead
options.consequence: You keep attacking a column that is now gathered and strong. The longer you push, the harder it can hit you back.

costs.resource: your whole company committed against a gathering force
costs.risk: the gathered column turns and destroys your company piece by piece

options.title: Shift to harassment
advantages: Slows the column without a full battle
Keeps your company safe while delaying the relief
Keeps the road dangerous for the enemy's whole march
disadvantages: Hit-and-run attacks slow the relief but do not stop it
A determined column pushes through given enough time
Trades a possible big win for a small but sure one
options.consequence: You stop trying to destroy the column and settle for slowing it down and bleeding it along the way.

costs.resource: you give up a big win in exchange for delay
costs.risk: the column shrugs off the attacks and finishes the relief late

options.title: Break off with the wreckage you have
advantages: Keeps the damage you already did and keeps your company whole
Avoids the risk of staying too long against a recovered enemy
Frees your company for the next job
disadvantages: The column, though hurt, may still finish the relief
Leaves the mission's main job only half done
Gives the road back to the enemy
options.consequence: You take the damage you have done and pull out, leaving the column hurt but not destroyed.

costs.resource: you end the operation early on purpose
costs.risk: the surviving column reaches the position and the relief succeeds anyway

entries.event: The column enters the high country and spreads out into small groups on the one road.
The first ambush hits. The column realizes it is under attack and starts to react.
Guards move toward the fighting, and the column's alert level rises.
The commander orders his groups to pull together into one force, so your window to pick them off one by one is closing.
The column is now gathered and alert. It either pushes through as one force or stops to clear the road carefully.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Destroy the column before its groups pull together. Once it fights as one full battalion, your company can no longer win, because it can no longer fight the enemy a few units at a time.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} relief column, battalion strength strung out on the march: 24-30 'Mechs of mixed weight (30-75 tons, Regular with a Veteran escort element) interspersed with a heavy tracked supply and bridging train and combat-vehicle escorts (vehicleShare covers the supply train and the armored vehicles guarding it). On the march the column cannot gather together. Under repeated ambush it pulls its groups closer, pushes guards to the threatened ends, and changes from an easy target into a force that fights back. Cut-off groups fight where they stand. Once gathered, the column pushes through.
opforSketch.behavior: A column moving to reinforce, reacting to attacks the way a good march commander does. It pulls its groups together, protects its supply, and refuses to be destroyed a few units at a time once it sees the threat. Its weakness is the road. Its strength is staying disciplined and gathering together before the road gets it killed.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN MARCH
forks.trigger: The column is destroyed or scattered on the road and the relief fails to reach the position.
forks.consequence: The contested position goes unreinforced and falls to {EMPLOYER}'s waiting force; the wrecked road becomes a graveyard that deters the next relief attempt.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY ROAD
forks.trigger: The column's supply and bridging are wrecked so thoroughly that no survivor can complete the relief.
forks.consequence: Not only does the relief fail, the enemy's ability to supply the sector by this route is broken for the campaign; {EMPLOYER} exploits a logistics collapse.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL COLUMN
forks.trigger: The column closes up and fights through, or the company is defeated in detail attempting too much.
forks.consequence: The relief reaches the contested position and reinforces it; the company withdraws having traded its ambush advantage for a fight it could not win, and the position {EMPLOYER} wanted is now strongly held.

storyElementSeed: A lance leader watches a stalled supply hauler lean against a frozen bank, its crew tiny and far below. She gives the order to blow the road behind it and trap it, before the guards can climb back into firing range.

phases.name: AMBUSH — THE FIRST BITE
phases.lead: Catch the column spread out and unready. Choose where to strike to shape how it reacts.

dataBlock.Column length: approximately 40 km, strung on one road
dataBlock.Column strength: one battalion: 'Mechs, supply trucks, bridge gear, and families
dataBlock.Order of march: roughly known from day-old intel, not exact
dataBlock.Alert state: low at start, rising with each contact

sidebarKernel.kernel: where the column's combat guards are placed, and how fast its alert level is rising toward the point where it pulls together.

phases.name: ISOLATE — CUTTING THE WORM
phases.lead: Drop obstacles to trap groups, then destroy the cut-off groups before the guards can reach them.

routes.name: SWITCHBACKS
routes.desc: The sharp hairpin climbs where vehicles slow to a crawl.
routes.tradeoff: Great ambush spots, but a block here can trap your own force on the wrong side.

routes.name: DEFILES
routes.desc: The narrow passes where the road squeezes between rock walls.
routes.tradeoff: A single wreck can seal a pass and trap a group, but the walls also limit your own escape routes.

protocol.Ambush signal: Codeword WINTER GULLET triggers the set ambush on the group entering the kill zone.
protocol.Break-contact code: Codeword COLD ROAD pulls the ambush team out before the guards get within firing range.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — BEFORE IT CLOSES
phases.lead: Press your advantage while the column is still spread out. Decide when it has gathered too much strength to keep attacking safely.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the column has gathered enough that you can no longer pick it off group by group, and whether to press, run hit-and-run attacks, or take your gains and leave.

assetDetails.detail: Combat 'Mechs and armored vehicles protecting the march. Alone, they are easy prey. Gathered together, they are a fight your company cannot win. Your whole plan depends on hitting them before they gather.
This is what makes the relief matter. Wreck it and the relief fails even if the 'Mechs get through. But it travels in the column's well-guarded middle, which is hard to reach.

title: OPERATION GRAVEL VEIN
skeleton: a route-security force too small for the road must keep convoys flowing through a canalized ambush corridor it cannot cover whole, where the irregular enemy owns the time and place, salts the road itself with mines and demolitions, and reads the security force's dispositions to strike the gaps - and a road patrolled to perfection with no convoys getting through is the failure
inspiration: main-supply-route security against an ambush corridor - the counter-IED convoy fight of a contested highway, Iraq, 2004-2007
situation: One road keeps {EMPLOYER}'s forward force on {WORLD} fed and fueled. {TARGET_FACTION}'s loyalist irregulars have turned its worst stretch into a killing ground for convoys. The supply route runs sixty kilometers through {DISTRICT}. The middle thirty kilometers is the danger zone. There the road is boxed in by high ground, river cuts, and empty roadside villages, which gives an ambusher every advantage. The irregulars do not hold the road. They pick the moment. They mine a culvert, blow a bridge, or shoot up a convoy from a tree line, then vanish. They have made the stretch so costly that the forward force is starting to cut back on what it sends. Your company runs route security. The core problem: you cannot cover all thirty kilometers at once. The ambushers pick when and where to strike, so all you control is how you spread out your force. Patrol constantly and you wear out your people guarding a road the enemy simply hits the day you go thin. Escort every convoy in strength and you can only run a few, so the forward force starves on a set schedule instead of by ambush. Your intelligence on the irregulars is a map of where they have struck before. It helps you guess, but it cannot promise anything, because a smart ambusher never repeats himself. The irregulars have a few light 'Mechs and homemade gun-vehicles they bring out for the bigger convoys. The rest is mines, demolition charges, and fighters who fade into ground they have lived on their whole lives. You have to keep the road open. Open means convoys getting through, not a road you patrolled for nothing.

objectives.primary: Keep {EMPLOYER}'s supply route open through the danger zone. Convoys must reach the forward force fast enough to keep it fighting.
objectives.secondary: Hit the ambush teams along the road - the mine-layers, the demolition cells, the gun-vehicles - hard enough that the forward force no longer has to ration its convoys.
objectives.bonus: Corner and destroy the irregulars' light 'Mechs. They are the one threat that can stop a convoy dead instead of just bleeding it.

complications.name: Thirty Kilometers, One Company
complications.text: You cannot cover the whole thirty kilometers at once. Wherever you mass your force, the rest of the road is open. The ambushers watch where you go and strike where you are not. Every choice of where to be is a choice of where not to be.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You have only enough force to guard part of the road at a time. Massing on one stretch leaves the others open, and the enemy hits the gaps you create.

complications.name: The Buried Road
complications.text: Mines and pre-set charges turn the road itself into the threat. A culvert wired to blow. A bridge weakened to drop under a heavy hauler. A charge in the shoulder set off by a passing vehicle. The enemy has spent weeks planting these, and clearing them is far slower than laying them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Stretches of road may hide mines or charges. Run a convoy without clearing first and you risk losing a vehicle and blocking the road. But clearing every kilometer is too slow to keep convoys moving fast enough.

complications.name: The Pattern That Lies
complications.text: Your map of past ambushes shows where the enemy has struck, not where he will strike next. Trusting that map too much is how a careful ambusher kills you. He knows you are studying his habits, so he hits the stretch your map calls safe.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Guessing ambush sites from past attacks only works up to a point. Lean on it too hard and you mass your company on a quiet stretch while a convoy gets hit somewhere else.

decisionPoints.name: How to Cover the Vein
decisionPoints.context: You cannot guard the whole road and run every convoy at full strength. Pick one. Your choice decides how much control you hand the enemy.

options.title: Heavy escort, fewer convoys
advantages: Each convoy is well guarded and likely to get through
Puts your strength right where the supplies are
Forces the ambushers to fight real combat power to score a hit
disadvantages: You can only escort a few convoys this heavily
The forward force gets less than it needs and has to ration
The road sits open to the enemy between convoy runs
options.consequence: You guard what moves, but not enough moves. The forward force feels the shortage.

costs.resource: Fewer convoys get through.
costs.risk: The forward force runs short on supplies and its operations slow down.

options.title: Constant route domination
advantages: Patrols and outposts fight for the whole stretch around the clock
Convoys move freely while you hold the road
Keeps the irregulars from moving where they please
disadvantages: Wears out the company trying to hold ground it cannot fully cover
The moment you thin out anywhere, the enemy hits that gap
Spreads your force so thin that no one point is strong
options.consequence: You try to hold the whole road and find it is longer than your company can cover. The enemy finds the gaps.

costs.resource: The company is worn thin across the whole road.
costs.risk: A thinned stretch gets ambushed and a convoy is caught where you are not.

options.title: Bait and counter-ambush
advantages: Uses a convoy as bait to pull an ambush onto ground you have already set up
Turns the enemy's habit of striking first against him
Can wipe out an ambush cell instead of just scaring it off
disadvantages: Puts the bait convoy at risk if your trap fails
Only works until the irregulars catch on and stop taking the bait
Only works if you guess right about where he will strike
options.consequence: You dangle a target and try to ambush the ambusher. You are betting your guess against his caution.

costs.resource: One convoy is put at risk as bait.
costs.risk: The irregulars refuse the bait, or hit it where you are not set up, and the bait convoy takes the loss.

decisionPoints.name: A Convoy in the Kill Zone
decisionPoints.context: A convoy is ambushed halfway down the road. A bridge drops behind it, the lead vehicle is burning, and fire is pouring down from the high ground. The escort is pinned in the fight, and the rest of your company is kilometers away.

options.title: Push the trapped convoy through
advantages: Gets the surviving vehicles out of the ambush fast
Denies the ambushers a long, drawn-out fight
Keeps the supplies moving toward the forward force
disadvantages: Getting past a dropped bridge may not even be possible
Leaves damaged vehicles and their crews behind
The convoy has to run through heavy fire to escape
options.consequence: You drive the survivors out and leave the wrecks and the ambushers behind you.

costs.resource: Damaged vehicles and their cargo are left behind.
costs.risk: The road ahead is blocked too, trapping the convoy between two cuts.

options.title: Fight to fix and reinforce
advantages: Pins the ambushers in place so the rest of your company can close in
A chance to wipe out the ambush cell, not just survive it
Recovers the damaged vehicles and crews if you win the fight
disadvantages: Your reinforcements are kilometers and minutes away
The pinned convoy keeps taking losses while it waits
The ambushers may slip away before help arrives
options.consequence: You turn the ambush into a battle and race your reinforcements against the convoy running out of time.

costs.resource: The convoy is held in the ambush zone while it waits for help.
costs.risk: Your company arrives to find the convoy destroyed and the ambushers gone.

options.title: Cover the withdrawal, abandon the run
advantages: Saves the most crews and escorts you can
Cuts your losses on a convoy already in a hopeless spot
Keeps the company strong for the next run
disadvantages: You lose the convoy's cargo completely
You hand the ambush site and the road to the enemy
A lost convoy makes the forward force's shortage worse
options.consequence: You give up the run to save the people, and the forward force goes without what was on those trucks.

costs.resource: A whole convoy's cargo is lost.
costs.risk: The abandoned cargo ends up arming or supplying the irregulars who grab it.

entries.event: The operation begins. You set your convoy pace, and the enemy's baseline of ambushes is in place.
The irregulars probe where you are weak. They strike a stretch you left thin to learn your habits.
Your convoy wins and losses decide the forward force's supply level. It either starts rationing or avoids it.
The irregulars send in their light 'Mechs against a major convoy. These are the one threat that can stop a run cold.
The forward force's next operation depends on how much supply the road has delivered by now.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: You must keep the road open through the whole contract. If too few convoys get through to meet the forward force's needs, its operations stall for lack of supply. That is the one measure that decides whether you succeeded or failed.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} loyalist irregular force optimized for route ambush: mining and demolition cells, foot ambush teams, a handful of improvised combat vehicles - haulers and technicals with bolted SRM and autocannon mounts - and a light 'Mech element of 3-5 machines (20-40 tons, Regular) held for the larger convoys (vehicleShare carries the gun-vehicles and the few 'Mechs). The irregulars never hold ground; they strike a convoy or a thinned patrol and melt away, bringing the 'Mechs out only when a target is worth the exposure and withdrawing them the moment a real fight develops. The mining teams and foot ambushers are the constant threat and field narratively.
opforSketch.behavior: Route interdiction by ambush and demolition. Own the time and place, read the security force's dispositions, strike the gaps, and bleed the convoys until the enemy rations himself. The light 'Mechs are the escalation that turns a bled convoy into a stopped one.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN VEIN
forks.trigger: Convoy throughput stays above the forward force's needs and the ambush capability is suppressed.
forks.consequence: The forward force stays supplied and mounts its operation on schedule; the vein quiets as the irregulars find the road too costly to work.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN GRAVEL
forks.trigger: The irregulars' light 'Mech element is pinned and destroyed and the ambush cells are broken.
forks.consequence: The route is not just open but safe; the freed security force can push the irregulars' support network back from the road entirely.

forks.name: OPERATION BLED WHITE
forks.trigger: Convoy losses force rationing and the forward force's supply falls below what it needs.
forks.consequence: The forward force's operation stalls for lack of supply and it is thrown onto the defensive; the vein becomes a no-go stretch and the irregulars own the road in fact.

storyElementSeed: An escort commander rides the cab of a lead hauler through the worst kilometer of the vein, watching a culvert ahead that looks like every other culvert, deciding whether the company has time to clear it or the convoy has time to wait while she does.

phases.name: POSTURE — COVERING THE VEIN
phases.lead: Lay out how the company will cover thirty kilometers it cannot hold whole, and set the convoy tempo against the ambush threat.

dataBlock.Coverage: one company - cannot be everywhere at once
dataBlock.Threat: mining and demolition cells, gun-vehicles, 3-5 light 'Mechs

sidebarKernel.kernel: how convoy throughput is tracking against the forward force's needs, and how close it is to forcing rationing.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE KILL ZONE
phases.lead: Run the convoys and answer the ambushes, deciding in the moment whether to push through, fix and reinforce, or cut losses.

routes.name: RIVER CUTS
routes.desc: Where the road runs canalized along the water.
routes.tradeoff: Fast and direct, but a dropped span here traps a convoy against the river with no detour.

routes.name: SETTLEMENT STRETCH
routes.desc: The road through the abandoned roadside hamlets.
routes.tradeoff: The buildings shorten the worst exposure, but they give foot ambushers cover right at the road's edge.

protocol.Convoy clearance call: Codeword GRAVEL VEIN releases a convoy onto the road once the lead stretch is checked.
protocol.Ambush response: Codeword HARD SHOULDER commits the nearest security element to a convoy in contact.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — KEEPING IT OPEN
phases.lead: Sustain the convoy tempo through the window and break the ambush capability before the forward force is starved.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the vein is staying open by the only measure that counts - supplies reaching the forward force - and whether the irregulars' 'Mechs can be cornered.

assetDetails.detail: The whole point of the operation; a road patrolled to perfection with no convoys getting through is a failure, and a convoy lost is supply the forward force does without.
Maintains the ambush pattern-of-life; warns that the map shows where the enemy has been and that betting on it is how a careful ambusher kills a careless escort.

title: OPERATION BORROWED COLORS
skeleton: a turned-force element must penetrate an insurgent network from inside using captured machines in enemy colors and defector-supplied recognition protocols, mapping cells and command links to roll the structure up in a night, where exposure accumulates with every contact and one wrong signal, known face, or defector's betrayal traps the disguised column deep in hostile ground among converging enemy 'Mechs
inspiration: the pseudo-operations of the Selous Scouts and Frank Kitson's counter-gangs - infiltrating an insurgency by wearing its face
situation: The best way into a hidden insurgent network is to pose as part of it. {EMPLOYER} has given your company captured enemy 'Mechs and orders to do exactly that. A {TARGET_FACTION} insurgency in {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} runs through cells your side cannot find. They meet at night, hide their gear in the city sprawl, and identify each other by recognition signals and word of mouth. A year of ordinary sweeps has caught foot soldiers but never touched the leadership that matters. So your company will pretend to be one of their own columns. You will use the captured 'Mechs painted in insurgent markings, a few defectors who know the recognition signals, and a cover story that you are a friendly unit passing through. The plan: make contact with cells, learn the hideout locations and the command links, then turn on them and destroy the whole network in one night. The danger is close and constant. One wrong signal, one cell that knows the fighter you are impersonating is dead, or one defector who only pretended to switch sides, and your cover is blown. Then you are a handful of 'Mechs deep in enemy ground with the real insurgent 'Mechs closing in. The defectors are your only key, and you cannot confirm they are loyal until a contact tests them. Your deception works only while no one looks closely, and these are people who look closely for a living. Learn the network, or die trying to reach it.

objectives.primary: Use the captured colors and defector signals to get inside the {TARGET_FACTION} insurgent network. Map its cells and command links, then destroy the network at the moment you choose.
objectives.secondary: Keep the deception intact long enough to reach the network's leaders, not just its outer cells.
objectives.bonus: Capture the network's leaders alive along with their records, which expose the support network across the district.

complications.name: A Face That Might Be Known
complications.text: The captured 'Mechs and the stolen identities belonged to real insurgents. The network may know those fighters are dead, or remember a habit of theirs you cannot copy. Your cover lasts only as long as no cell looks too closely at the column wearing its colors.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every contact with a cell carries a hidden chance of being exposed. More contacts, or any slip-up, raise that chance. Once the cover breaks, the mission turns into a fight deep in enemy ground.

complications.name: The Defector's True Heart
complications.text: A few defectors are your only key to the recognition signals. But a defector working for you may secretly still be working for them. The signal they hand you may be the correct one, or the one that marks you to the cell as an enemy.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You cannot confirm the defectors' signals are correct. A double-agent or a mistaken defector can give a wrong signal at a key contact, exposing the column at the worst moment.

complications.name: The Tightening Window
complications.text: Every night the deception runs, more of the network sees your column, and the odds rise that someone catches the lie. The deeper you go, the more you learn, but the more likely you are to be caught before you can strike.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The longer the mission runs, the more of the network you map, but the higher the total risk of exposure. Pushing for the leaders means trading a complete map against a rising chance of being caught first.

decisionPoints.name: How Deep to Push the Deception
decisionPoints.context: You can arrest the cells you have already found, push deeper toward the leaders, or do some of both. Every step deeper teaches you more and risks more.

options.title: Roll up the cells you have
advantages: Secures the cells you have already reached before exposure rises further
Lowest risk that the deception falls apart
Hurts the network for real, even if the leaders get away
disadvantages: The leaders escape and rebuild
The support network is left intact
A partial win that can grow back
options.consequence: You take the foot soldiers and the hideouts and let the leaders slip away. The network is hurt but not destroyed.

costs.resource: the leaders left free
costs.risk: the surviving leaders rebuild the network from its support base

options.title: Push for the command element
advantages: Targets the leaders, the only blow that ends the network
Captures the command links and the leadership
A complete kill if it works
disadvantages: Requires the longest, deepest time undercover
Every extra contact risks the cover
Failure deep in the network is a disaster, not a setback
options.consequence: You gamble the whole company on reaching the leaders before the network catches the lie.

costs.resource: the most exposure, for the decisive target
costs.risk: the cover breaks deep in the network and the company is trapped among the insurgent 'Mechs closing in

options.title: Plant a source, then withdraw clean
advantages: Uses your access to plant or recruit a long-term spy inside the network
Pulls the column out before exposure peaks
Gives lasting intelligence beyond this one mission
disadvantages: Gives up arresting the cells now
A planted spy can be found and turned against you
Needs patience an employer who wants results now may not have
options.consequence: You give up arrests now for a lasting window into the network, betting the spy stays hidden.

costs.resource: arrests given up to plant a spy
costs.risk: the spy is caught, which reveals the whole deception after the fact

decisionPoints.name: The Contact That Smells Wrong
decisionPoints.context: At a night meeting, a cell leader pauses over a recognition signal and starts asking questions only a real insurgent would know to ask. Your defector's answers are not convincing him. The situation is going bad.

options.title: Brazen it out
advantages: Keeps the deception alive if the bluff works
Avoids starting the fight too soon
Keeps your access if the cell leader's doubt fades
disadvantages: A failed bluff confirms his suspicion and blows the cover badly
Bets everything on out-talking a careful professional
No backup plan if the questions keep coming
options.consequence: You commit to the lie and find out whether nerve beats a careful man's instinct.

costs.resource: the deception bet on one bluff
costs.risk: the bluff fails and the cell raises the alarm while the column is surrounded

options.title: Strike first, take this cell
advantages: Acts first, before the alarm spreads
Captures this cell while you can still reach it
Ends the uncertainty on your terms
disadvantages: Reveals the deception early, so the rest of the network hides
Gives up the deeper command links
Turns a quiet infiltration into an open fight
options.consequence: You take what is in front of you and accept that the network now knows it was infiltrated.

costs.resource: the deeper network warned and lost
costs.risk: the alarm reaches the insurgent 'Mechs before the company can pull out

options.title: Break contact, withdraw the column
advantages: Pulls out before the doubt becomes certainty
Saves the company and what it has already learned
Leaves room to try another approach later
disadvantages: A column that suddenly leaves a meeting looks suspicious itself
Gives up this cell and possibly the whole mission
May confirm the cell leader's doubt as you leave
options.consequence: You break off and hope a calm exit reads as caution, not guilt, keeping what you have.

costs.resource: the contact, and maybe the mission, given up
costs.risk: leaving confirms the suspicion and the network locks down the district behind you

entries.event: The column enters the district in borrowed colors; the cover story is in play.
First cell contact; the recognition protocols are tested for the first time.
The network passes the column inward toward deeper cells. The risk of exposure starts to build.
A command link comes within reach, and with it the greatest risk of exposure yet.
The total risk peaks. The network is close to catching a slip-up. The moment to strike or pull out has come.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Destroy the network, or get out, before the cover is blown. Once the deception fails, the company is a handful of 'Mechs deep in enemy ground with the full insurgent force closing in.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} insurgent network, cellular and elusive: dozens of foot fighters in compartmented cells, a support apparatus in the sprawl, and a 'Mech element of 4-6 light and medium machines (25-50 tons, Regular) hidden between actions, plus improvised gun-vehicles (vehicleShare carries the technicals and the few 'Mechs once the fight is open). While the deception holds, the network is invisible and the threat is discovery, not combat. Once the cover is blown, the hidden 'Mechs and gun-vehicles converge fast on the exposed column, and the cells fight to fix it until they arrive. The foot fighters field narratively.
opforSketch.behavior: A careful underground that survives by keeping its cells separate and its recognition signals strict. Its strength is suspicion. It tests every contact and passes strangers up the chain only once satisfied. Provoked, it quickly concentrates its hidden combat power on the threat, moving fast because it knows the ground.

forks.name: OPERATION FALSE DAWN
forks.trigger: The network's cells and command links are mapped and rolled up before the cover is blown.
forks.consequence: The insurgency is broken at the root and {EMPLOYER} pacifies the district far more cheaply than a year of sweeps managed; the captured links expose cells on neighboring worlds.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN LEDGER
forks.trigger: The network's leadership is taken alive with its records, exposing the support apparatus across the district.
forks.consequence: The entire support structure is unrolled from the captured records; {EMPLOYER} dismantles the insurgency's logistics and turns the intelligence into a regional counter-network campaign.

forks.name: OPERATION DEAD GIVEAWAY
forks.trigger: The cover is blown deep in the network, by a known face, a wrong signal, or a defector's betrayal.
forks.consequence: The company is exposed in hostile ground with the insurgent 'Mechs converging; it fights a desperate extraction out of the district, and the network, now wise to the tactic, hardens against it forever.

storyElementSeed: A MechWarrior sits in a cockpit painted in another faction's colors. A defector trades passwords with a shape in the dark. The pilot counts the seconds, very quietly, waiting to see whether the shape waves them forward or reaches for a radio.

phases.name: INGRESS — WEARING THE FACE
phases.lead: Enter the district in the captured colors and make the first cell contact. This tests whether the deception will hold at all.

dataBlock.Cover: captured 'Mechs in insurgent markings, defector-supplied protocols
dataBlock.Cover story: a friendly insurgent element displacing through the district
dataBlock.Network: compartmented cells, hidden 'Mechs, a support apparatus
dataBlock.Key intelligence: the defectors - reliability unverifiable until tested

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the recognition signals are working, and which defectors give signals that pass cleanly versus which draw questions.

phases.name: PENETRATION — UP THE CHAIN
phases.lead: Let the network pass the column inward toward its leaders, learning cells and hideouts as the risk of exposure quietly rises.

routes.name: NIGHT MEETS
routes.desc: The cell-to-cell contacts in the dark.
routes.tradeoff: Each meeting teaches you more of the network, but each is also a chance for a face or a signal to give you away.

routes.name: CACHE RUNS
routes.desc: Trips to the network's supply and rally sites.
routes.tradeoff: They reveal the supply setup worth destroying, but they put the column where the network watches most closely.

protocol.Recognition: Defector-supplied night signals, contact by contact; a wrong one marks the column as enemy.
protocol.Abort code: Codeword BORROWED COLORS, passed in clear, drops the deception and triggers the fight or the run.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE TURN
phases.lead: Choose the moment to destroy the network or pull out, before the rising odds of exposure choose it for you.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the leaders are within reach, and whether the cover will hold one more contact or has already started to fail.

assetDetails.detail: The only key to the recognition signals, and the biggest risk you cannot check. Their knowledge opens the network, and their loyalty is tested at every contact.
The disguise the whole mission rests on. Convincing from a distance, but dangerous up close, where a recognized machine or a wrong marking can blow the cover in seconds.

title: OPERATION TWO-WAY STREET
skeleton: an escort force must shepherd its own resupply convoys forward along the single shared two-way artery that also carries the enemy's return traffic, and is ordered to interdict that return traffic on the same road, so every ambush it springs halts its own throughput and every safe run it makes teaches the watcher its timing, against a former-allied garrison that knows the road and the schedule it used to share
inspiration: the two-way Burma Road / Ledo Road logistics fight where the same artery served friend and foe in turn
situation: Only one road in {DISTRICT} is good enough to matter, and on {WORLD} both sides must use it. {EMPLOYER}'s forward brigade depends on the fuel and ammunition your convoys push up the highway. The {TARGET_FACTION} garrison at the far end runs its own supply back down the same road, because the ground on either side is too broken for tracked vehicles. Your contract gives you two jobs at once: keep your convoys moving forward, and cut the enemy's traffic coming back. Those two jobs work against each other. To stop the enemy, you must halt, set an ambush, and turn a stretch of road into a battle. That same stretch is then blocked for your own next convoy. To run your convoys safely, you keep the road quiet and moving, which is exactly the calm the enemy's supply runs need too. Worse, this garrison held the road a month ago, when it was on your side. Its officers know your convoy timings, your overnight stops, and your refuel halts, because those used to be theirs. They do not have to guess your routine. They remember it. Your read on the enemy's schedule is a day old and built from sensor sweeps a clever quartermaster can fake, so you are guessing their runs while they recall yours. You must feed your brigade and starve theirs on one road, and the road does not care whose convoy is on it.

objectives.primary: Keep {EMPLOYER}'s forward brigade supplied at the rate it needs. Run convoys forward through {DISTRICT} on the shared highway.
objectives.secondary: Cut the {TARGET_FACTION} garrison's supply runs on the same road, down below the level that keeps its position going.
objectives.bonus: Capture an enemy fuel or ammunition convoy intact instead of wrecking it, turning the enemy's supplies into your own.

complications.name: The Road You Both Need
complications.text: An ambush you spring blocks the road with wreckage and fire. That blocked road is the one your own next convoy was due on. Every ambush you mount cuts your own supply flow for as long as the burning wrecks block the road. You cannot fight on the road and run it in the same hour.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Running an ambush on a road segment closes that segment to your convoys while it is cleared. A convoy due through a blocked segment must wait, or detour onto rough ground that costs it time and vehicles.

complications.name: They Wrote Your Schedule
complications.text: The enemy commanders ran these convoy timings themselves a month ago. The overnight stops, the dawn refuel halt, the slow climb up the ridge - they know all of it, because it used to be their routine. Your routine is not a secret you can keep. They already remember it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The enemy can predict your convoy timing without any scouting. Repeating any convoy routine sharply raises the chance the next run is ambushed at a known weak point, unless you deliberately change the schedule at a cost.

complications.name: Traffic That Lies
complications.text: Their supply runs hide inside ordinary traffic - a fuel truck disguised as a civilian tanker, an ammunition hauler painted like a farm convoy. Telling military traffic worth an ambush from civilians you are forbidden to fire on is the difference between a clean strike and a massacre on the road.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Enemy supply vehicles are mixed in with civilian traffic. Ambushing the wrong target wastes the ambush, and if the target is civilian, it costs you reputation and a contract penalty.

decisionPoints.name: Feed or Starve First
decisionPoints.context: You cannot run your convoys and ambush theirs in the same window on the same road. The balance you strike sets which brigade goes hungry.

options.title: Prioritize friendly throughput
advantages: Your brigade stays fully supplied and able to fight
Keeps the road quiet and moving for your runs
Lowest risk to your own convoys
disadvantages: The enemy garrison resupplies untouched
Gives up the interdiction half of the order entirely
A well-fed enemy is harder to beat when your brigade attacks
options.consequence: Your side fights well-stocked, but so does the enemy, and the interdiction job goes undone.

costs.resource: enemy resupply allowed
costs.risk: the enemy garrison stockpiles for a counterattack your interdiction was meant to prevent

options.title: Prioritize interdiction
advantages: Starves the enemy garrison toward collapse
Serves the offensive purpose behind the contract
Forces the enemy to fight short on supplies
disadvantages: Blocks the road to your own convoys again and again
Your brigade starts rationing as fewer supplies get through
Turns the highway into a battlefield you also depend on
options.consequence: The enemy goes hungry, and step by step so does the brigade you are supposed to feed.

costs.resource: your own supply flow sacrificed
costs.risk: the forward brigade runs short and its own operation stalls for lack of supply

options.title: Alternate by window
advantages: Runs convoys in one time slot and ambushes in the next, sharing the road by schedule
Keeps both halves of the order partly done
Denies the enemy a fixed sense of when the road is dangerous
disadvantages: Demands tight timing the tired company may not keep up
A slipped time slot sends a convoy into an ambush you set
Neither job is done at full strength
options.consequence: You split the road between feeding and fighting, and survive by never confusing the two time slots.

costs.resource: timing discipline stretched thin
costs.risk: a mistimed slot puts a friendly convoy into a kill zone meant for the enemy

decisionPoints.name: An Enemy Convoy in Reach
decisionPoints.context: Your scouts spot a {TARGET_FACTION} fuel convoy on a stretch you can reach. You can wreck it, try to capture it intact, or let it pass to keep the road open for your own run due within the hour.

options.title: Destroy it on the road
advantages: Denies the enemy the fuel for certain
A fast ambush, over before escorts can gather
No risk of a capture attempt going wrong
disadvantages: Burning wreckage blocks the road to your own next convoy
Destroyed fuel is fuel neither side gets
Reveals your ambush position for the rest of the day
options.consequence: The enemy loses the fuel and you lose the road for a while, and your quartermaster notes the supplies you cost yourself.

costs.resource: the road blocked by wreckage
costs.risk: your own convoy backs up behind the burning column you just created

options.title: Take it intact
advantages: Captured fuel and vehicles become your own supply
Hurts the enemy and resupplies you at the same time
The best possible payoff from an ambush
disadvantages: Taking a convoy intact means a close fight that risks the prize
Captured vehicles must be driven out under guard, tying up your force
A capture gone wrong leaves you fighting in the open for nothing
options.consequence: You try to turn the enemy's supplies into your own, betting the close fight does not burn the prize.

costs.resource: force tied up guarding captured vehicles
costs.risk: the capture fight sets off the fuel and you lose the convoy and your ambushers both

options.title: Let it pass, run your own
advantages: Keeps the road open for your scheduled convoy
Keeps your own supplies flowing when they are due
Hides your ambush ability for a better target
disadvantages: The enemy fuel reaches its garrison untouched
Passing up an easy target looks like a missed mission
The enemy learns this stretch is safe to run
options.consequence: You protect your own run and let the enemy's go, putting your brigade's supply ahead of the enemy's.

costs.resource: an easy ambush passed up
costs.risk: the enemy convoy you let past supplies the unit that later attacks your brigade

entries.event: The operation opens. Your convoys and the enemy's supply runs are both moving on the shared road.
The enemy, using timings he remembers, probes one of your known overnight stops to check the old routine still holds.
Your first ambush blocks a road segment. The next friendly convoy must wait or detour while the wreckage burns.
Both brigades' supply levels show the effect of sharing the road. Whoever has rationed harder starts to feel it in the field.
The enemy changes his convoy schedule to break the routine he thinks you have learned. The fight for the road reaches its decisive stage.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: By the end of the contracted window, your brigade must be supplied above its fighting level and the enemy's must not. If instead the road has fed both sides equally, neither the escort nor the ambushing has decided anything.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} garrison that runs and guards its own supply convoys. The road escort is 6-9 medium 'Mechs (40-65 tons, Regular, with a Veteran command lance that once ran this very road), plus a fast screen of hover and wheeled scouts and gun-trucks guarding the convoys (vehicleShare carries the escorts and the supply vehicles themselves). The escorts react quickly to an ambush on their convoy and push hard to clear the road they also need. They break off an ambush of their own if it costs more than about 30% of the escort. The convoy drivers and depot infantry are handled in the story, not on the table.
opforSketch.behavior: The enemy fights the same supply war you do, in reverse. He protects his own runs, harasses yours, and uses the road timings he remembers from when he held the route. He fights for the road as a shared resource, not to destroy your company, and he counts on your two-part order splitting your effort against itself.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL TANKS
forks.trigger: The forward brigade stays supplied and the enemy garrison's resupply is cut below its sustaining threshold.
forks.consequence: The brigade attacks well-stocked into a starved garrison; {EMPLOYER} exploits a supply imbalance the shared road was supposed to deny it.

forks.name: OPERATION CAPTURED COLUMN
forks.trigger: An enemy fuel or ammunition convoy is taken intact and added to friendly stocks.
forks.consequence: The enemy's own logistics swell your brigade's reserves; the captured stores let {EMPLOYER} extend its offensive past where its supply tail alone would have culminated.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY ROAD
forks.trigger: Friendly throughput collapses under the road's split use, or the enemy keeps its convoys running while yours stall.
forks.consequence: The forward brigade rations and goes onto the defensive while the enemy garrison stays fed; the shared road becomes the enemy's road in fact, and the interdiction mission is a write-off.

storyElementSeed: A convoy commander waits with her lead hauler at a refuel halt her enemy named years ago. She watches the tree line that always hid the lookouts, knowing the men up there learned this stop from the same manual she did.

phases.name: POSTURE — SHARING THE ROAD
phases.lead: Balance running your own convoys against cutting the enemy's on one two-way road, knowing the enemy already knows your schedule.

dataBlock.Friendly need: the forward brigade's daily supply requirement
dataBlock.Enemy traffic: garrison supply runs on the same road, timing partly known
dataBlock.Routine risk: the enemy ran these timings last month
