phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE AMBUSH AND THE RUN
phases.lead: Ambush enemy traffic and push your own convoys through, never letting the two meet on the shared road.

routes.name: ESCARPMENT GRIND
routes.desc: The slow climb where every convoy crawls.
routes.tradeoff: The natural kill zone for both sides. Whoever ambushes here scores, but the wreckage blocks the climb for everyone.

routes.name: VALLEY RUN
routes.desc: The fast, open lowland stretch.
routes.tradeoff: Quick and easy to drive, but the open ground lets escorts and ambushers fire at long range with no cover.

protocol.Convoy release: Codeword TWO-WAY clears a friendly convoy onto the road once the first stretch reads quiet.
protocol.Ambush call: Codeword CROSS TRAFFIC springs a prepared ambush on enemy supply traffic in the kill zone, and blocks that segment to friendly runs.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — WHO EATS
phases.lead: Keep your brigade fed and starve the enemy's across the window, deciding when an enemy convoy is worth blocking your own road to take.

sidebarKernel.kernel: whether the supply balance is tipping toward your brigade or the enemy's, and whether the road can serve both halves of the order one more day.

assetDetails.detail: The forward brigade's lifeline. Every hour the road is blocked by an ambush is supply they do without, and a lost convoy is a fight the brigade goes into short on gear.
Once ran this road for your side and remembers every timing. He does not need to scout your routine, only to recall it, and he counts on your two-part order splitting your effort.

title: OPERATION DRY WELL
skeleton: a raid force must seize an enemy fuel-and-cracking depot and run its pumps to drain the stockpile out before the depot's own split-loyalty workforce can sabotage the one irreplaceable refinery tower the instant the alarm trips, where burning the depot is the easy failure and keeping the works whole and pumping under guard is the whole problem, racing the demolition the keepers will trigger and the relief that will come
inspiration: the race to capture the Ploiesti oil refineries intact before the retreating keepers could fire the cracking towers, 1944
situation: This campaign runs on fuel, and the only refinery in {DISTRICT} that can produce heavy 'Mech-grade fuel sits in {TARGET_FACTION} hands on {WORLD}. {EMPLOYER} does not want it burned. {EMPLOYER} wants it working, and wants the full fuel tanks beside it drained into friendly tankers before the enemy can destroy either. The problem is the depot's own workers. The refinery crew - technicians, pump operators, line foremen - sided with the loyalists when the world split. They are still on the site, still running the plant under a thin enemy guard. The moment an alarm sounds, they have orders and the means to blow up the catalytic cracking tower, the one part that cannot be rebuilt anywhere short of a core world. That would turn the whole prize into scrap and start a fire that burns for a week. So you cannot fight your way in loudly, and you cannot shell the place. You must take the depot fast enough that the alarm never reaches the demolition team. Secure the cracking tower and the crew before anyone reaches a detonator. Then keep the pumps running, using that same enemy-held crew or your own techs, to empty the fuel tanks into your convoy while an enemy relief column races toward you. Your only read on which workers will sabotage and which will just quietly stop working comes from a defector, and it is a day old. Burn the depot and you have done the enemy's job for him. Take it whole and drain it, and you have fueled a campaign.

objectives.primary: Seize the fuel refinery with the catalytic cracking tower intact and undamaged, before the workers can sabotage it.
objectives.secondary: Run the pumps and drain the fuel tanks into {EMPLOYER}'s convoy before the relief column arrives.
objectives.bonus: Win over the refinery crew, or capture its key people, so the plant keeps producing for {EMPLOYER} after the raid instead of being drained just once.

complications.name: The Hand on the Detonator
complications.text: The cracking tower is wired with explosives, and the people who would set them off work the site every day. The whole raid depends on the alarm never reaching the demolition team. One radio call, or one foreman who sees armor at the fence and reaches for a switch, and the prize burns. Speed and silence are not options here. They are the mission.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If you breach the fence loudly or the alarm spreads, a demolition timer starts on the cracking tower. Reaching and securing the tower's control room before the timer runs out is a hard sub-objective. Fail it and you lose the bonus and most of the prize.

complications.name: A Workforce of Two Minds
complications.text: The crew sided with the loyalists when the world split, but a month under enemy guard changes minds. Some will stop working and step aside, some will run the pumps for you willingly, and some will sabotage on principle or on orders. You will not know which is which until the alarm tests them, and you need their hands to run the plant.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The crew is secretly divided. Take the site by cooperation and you get working pumps and a faster drain. Misjudge them or handle them roughly and the undecided ones turn to sabotage, which slows or blocks the drain.

complications.name: The Burning Road
complications.text: An enemy relief column starts down the road the moment the garrison learns the depot is hit. Draining the fuel tanks is slow work - hoses, pumps, and convoy trips measured in hours - and the relief is coming in those same hours. Every liter you pump is pumped against a clock with a battalion at the end of it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A relief force sets out when the alarm sounds and arrives on a fixed timeline. The longer you hold the site, the more fuel you drain, so there is a direct trade between fuel taken and the risk of being caught by the relief.

decisionPoints.name: How to Take the Depot
decisionPoints.context: You must reach the cracking tower before anyone can set off its charges. How you get through the fence decides whether the alarm reaches the detonator first.

options.title: Silent rush on the tower
advantages: A fast, quiet team drives straight for the cracking tower and its control room
Best chance to reach the demolition switch before the alarm spreads
Keeps the prize whole
disadvantages: A small fast team is exposed if it is spotted early
Skips the rest of the site, leaving enemy guards behind you
Everything depends on reaching one control room in time
options.consequence: You bet the mission on one fast strike at the thing that can ruin it, and accept the enemy guards left behind you.

costs.resource: the raid bet on one fast timed strike
costs.risk: the strike is spotted, the alarm wins, and the tower is blown

options.title: Cordon, then clear inward
advantages: Seals the depot so no demolition team or messenger escapes
Clearing step by step cuts enemy resistance before you reach the tower
Controls the whole site, not just the control room
disadvantages: Slower, so the alarm has time to reach the demolition team
Sealing the site is visible and loud, the very trigger you fear
Time spent clearing is time the tower stays wired to blow
options.consequence: You take the site properly and gamble that sealing it fast enough keeps the detonator out of reach.

costs.resource: time spent while the tower stays wired to blow
costs.risk: the slow approach gives a foreman the seconds he needs to set off the charge

options.title: Turn the crew first
advantages: A defector reaching the loyalist crew may get the charges disabled from inside
A cooperating crew means working pumps from the first minute
Avoids a race against a timer that never starts
disadvantages: Depends entirely on the defector judging who can be reached
A contact that betrays you triggers the very sabotage you meant to prevent
Takes setup time and a quiet approach before the raid
options.consequence: You try to win the tower before a shot is fired, betting the crew is as loyal as the defector swears.

costs.resource: a quiet approach to the crew before the raid
costs.risk: the contact is exposed and the crew blows the tower to prove its new loyalty

decisionPoints.name: How Long to Pump
decisionPoints.context: The fuel tanks are full and the relief is coming. Every hour spent draining means more fuel for the campaign, and one hour closer to a battalion at your fence.

options.title: Drain it dry
advantages: Takes the most fuel possible - a campaign's worth
Empties the prize so the enemy gets nothing back
The best supply payoff available
disadvantages: Holds the site until the relief is almost on top of you
A long drain means a hard fight to break away
Risks losing the loaded convoy to the relief at the end
options.consequence: You take it all and bet you can break away with full tankers before the relief closes the trap.

costs.resource: the site held until the relief nearly arrives
costs.risk: the relief arrives before the convoy clears and the fuel you took is recaptured or burned

options.title: Pump a safe load and go
advantages: Takes a solid share of the fuel with time to spare for withdrawal
Breaks away before the relief arrives
Keeps the convoy and the force safe
disadvantages: Leaves fuel in the tanks for the enemy to recover
A partial drain is a partial result
Cuts the campaign's windfall short
options.consequence: You take what you can carry safely and leave the rest, trading fuel for a clean getaway.

costs.resource: fuel left in the tanks
costs.risk: the fuel you leave is recovered and supplies the enemy you were trying to starve

options.title: Drain, then deny the rest
advantages: Takes a useful load, then destroys the leftover fuel so the enemy gets nothing
Balances a real haul against denying the rest
Leaves the cracking tower intact if you only burn the leftover fuel
disadvantages: Setting the fires adds time at the worst moment
Fire near half-full tanks risks the whole site, tower included
A fire that spreads destroys the prize you were sparing
options.consequence: You carry off a load and burn what is left, betting the fire stays in the tanks and off the tower.

costs.resource: extra minutes to set fires as the relief nears
costs.risk: the fire spreads to the cracking tower and you lose the plant after all

entries.event: The raid team reaches the depot fence. The workers are on shift and the cracking tower stands wired to blow.
Contact or an alarm decides the demolition timer. If it starts, the race for the control room is on.
The site is either secured or not. The pumps begin filling the convoy, with the crew either willing or forced.
The enemy garrison's relief column is confirmed on the road, its arrival timed and counting down.
The fuel tanks are mostly drained. The choice to keep pumping or break away comes due against the relief.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break away with the fuel before the relief column arrives and pins you at the site. Once it does, the loaded convoy and the raid force are both fighting to survive on ground you cannot hold.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} depot guard backed by a relief column: on site, a light guard of 3-5 'Mechs (25-45 tons, Regular) and a security-vehicle slice covering the perimeter and the gates (vehicleShare carries the guard vehicles and gate defenses), too light to stop a determined raid but enough to raise the alarm and cover the demolition party. The relief is a reinforced company of 9-12 medium and heavy 'Mechs (45-75 tons, Regular with a Veteran lead) that drives hard for the depot on alarm. The refinery workforce and demolition party are infantry and field narratively, but the demolition threat to the cracking tower is the operation's central danger.
opforSketch.behavior: The guard's job is to trip the alarm and buy the demolition team time, not to win. It fights to delay you and to let the tower be destroyed. The relief drives to recapture the depot or, failing that, to destroy it and trap the raiders, pressing hard once it arrives.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL BOWSER
forks.trigger: The depot is taken with the cracking tower intact and a substantial fuel load is drained and withdrawn before the relief arrives.
forks.consequence: A campaign's worth of reaction mass reaches {EMPLOYER}'s forces; the fuel lets the offensive press on, and the intact refinery becomes a prize worth coming back to hold.

forks.name: OPERATION WORKING WELL
forks.trigger: The cracking tower is taken intact and the crew is secured cooperatively, so the works can keep producing for {EMPLOYER} after the raid.
forks.consequence: Not just the fuel but the refinery itself is turned; {EMPLOYER} gains a producing source of 'Mech-grade reaction mass and the strategic edge of denying it to the enemy for good.

forks.name: OPERATION PILLAR OF FIRE
forks.trigger: The cracking tower is fired, or the relief arrives and pins the raid before the fuel is withdrawn.
forks.consequence: The refinery burns or is recaptured and the raid force fights its way out empty, or worse; the one source of heavy reaction mass in the district is denied to both sides, and the campaign's fuel problem gets harder for everyone.

storyElementSeed: A raid leader stands in the shadow of the cracking tower, looking up at the explosive charge taped to a feed line. Nearby, a pump foreman who has not yet chosen a side waits to be told whether to start the pumps or run.

phases.name: INGRESS — THE PERIMETER
phases.lead: Reach the depot and break in fast enough that the alarm never reaches the demolition team at the cracking tower.

dataBlock.Prize: fuel refinery; the catalytic cracking tower cannot be replaced
dataBlock.Threat to the prize: workers ready to sabotage the moment an alarm sounds
dataBlock.Relief: a reinforced company arriving on a fixed timer from the alarm

sidebarKernel.kernel: which workers the defector thinks will quit, run the pumps, or reach for the detonator, and how old that read is.

phases.name: GROUND — THE PUMPS
phases.lead: Secure the cracking tower and the crew, get the pumps filling the convoy, and drain the fuel tanks against the relief's timer.

routes.name: TANK FARM
routes.desc: The full storage tanks and the pump house.
routes.tradeoff: Where the fuel is and where the pumps run. Holding it drains the prize, but a fire here ends everything.

routes.name: CONTROL GALLERY
routes.desc: The cracking tower's demolition control room.
routes.tradeoff: Taking it stops the tower from being blown, but it sits at the most heavily defended heart of the plant.

protocol.Tower secure call: Codeword DRY WELL confirms the cracking tower's charges are disarmed and the pumps may run.
protocol.Crew handling: Codeword OPEN VALVE means the workers are cooperating and the drain is at full speed.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — BEFORE THE RELIEF
phases.lead: Break away with the loaded convoy before the relief column pins you, deciding how much fuel is worth the closing timer.

sidebarKernel.kernel: how much of the fuel is drained, how close the relief has come, and whether one more convoy trip is worth the risk of the trap closing.

assetDetails.detail: Loyalist at heart, but enemy-guarded for a month and secretly divided until the alarm tests them. Their hands run the pumps, and their hands wired the tower. The raid needs the first and fears the second.
The one part that cannot be replaced anywhere in the district. It is both the prize and the trap, wired to burn, and every choice in the raid turns on keeping it whole.

title: OPERATION SLACK WATER RUN
skeleton: a relief convoy of lightly armed lighters must run a tightening in-system patrol blockade to a besieged orbital base on a recharge-window clock, threading only the sensor-shadow lanes the picket's own geometry leaves open, where each successful pass teaches the blockade to close the lane it used and the base's hold-out clock runs shorter than the safe passages allow
inspiration: the Malta convoys running an Axis blockade to a besieged island, 1942 - the run, not the siege
situation: A garrison on an airless moon is still holding out, but only because supply ships keep sneaking in. The garrison belongs to {EMPLOYER}, and the moon orbits {WORLD}. A {TARGET_FACTION} force has sealed the garrison off. Their warships and fighters ring the moon and block the way to the surface. The garrison has only a few days of reactor fuel and ammunition left. Your job is to break through the blockade. You will guide a group of lightly armed supply ships and one 'Mech-carrying lander past the enemy line to the base. Then you do it again and again, until the siege breaks or the base falls. The supply ships cannot win a fight. One enemy warship outguns your whole group. Your only edge is to slip through gaps the enemy cannot watch: the sensor blind spots behind the moon, a field of floating debris, and the seams where the enemy's patrol orbits leave an opening. Your navigator can find these gaps. The catch is that the enemy learns. Use a gap once and get through, and they cover it before your next trip. So each run must use a new gap, and each new gap is tighter than the last. Worse, the base will run out of supplies before you run out of safe gaps. Your map of the enemy patrol is already hours old and getting worse, because they keep shifting their line on purpose to ruin your planning. You are trying to feed people who may not last long enough for the supplies to reach them.

objectives.primary: Get supply ships through the {TARGET_FACTION} blockade to the besieged base. Deliver the reactor fuel and ammunition before the garrison runs out.
objectives.secondary: Land the 'Mech reinforcements at the base. With them, the garrison can attack the siege from the ground.
objectives.bonus: Damage or drive off one enemy warship. This opens a gap the enemy cannot quickly close, which makes every later run safer.

complications.name: A Lane Used Is a Lane Lost
complications.text: The enemy learns from every run. You might slip through a sensor blind spot, a gap in the debris, or a seam in their orbits. But use any gap once, and the enemy covers it before your next run. So each run must find a new gap, and each new one is tighter. There are only so many gaps.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each successful run closes the gap it used. The next run must use a worse gap, so the risk of getting caught climbs with every trip. Eventually no safe gap is left, and a run must either fight through or turn back.

complications.name: The Lighters Cannot Fight
complications.text: The supply ships carry almost no weapons. If an enemy warship spots the group, it can tear the ships apart before your escort can reach them. Staying hidden is the only real defense. If that fails, the escort has to buy time it usually does not have.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The supply ships are fragile and cannot trade fire with enemy warships. If the enemy intercepts them, the escort must cover a retreat or a push through. A supply ship caught in the open is likely lost along with its cargo.

complications.name: The Shorter Clock
complications.text: The base needs more deliveries than there are safe gaps left to make them. It will run out of supplies before you run out of gaps. So at some point you must run through a gap that is not safe, or the base falls while you wait for one that is.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The garrison needs more deliveries than there are low-risk runs available. To finish the resupply, you must accept at least one high-risk run through a covered gap. If you refuse, the base runs out of supplies and falls.

decisionPoints.name: How to Run the Blockade
decisionPoints.context: Every run forces a trade: stealth against speed, and safety against how much cargo you move. The method you pick decides how the enemy can respond.

options.title: Stealth runs, minimum emission
advantages: Best chance of slipping through a gap unseen
Protects the supply ships and their cargo
Keeps the enemy guessing where your next run will go
disadvantages: Slow, quiet approaches mean fewer runs in the time you have
Only one delivery per trip, against a fast clock
One detection turns a quiet run into a massacre
options.consequence: You move slow and quiet and deliver only a little at a time. You are betting that little adds up before the base falls.

costs.resource: less cargo delivered, in trade for staying hidden
costs.risk: too few deliveries get through and the base falls while waiting

options.title: Fast dash, escort forward
advantages: You carry more cargo per run because you move fast and take more risk
The escort rides up front to scare off or soak up an attack
You get supplies to the base sooner, which matters against its short clock
disadvantages: Moving fast and loud makes the enemy spot you sooner
You risk the escort in a fight you meant to avoid
If the run fails, you can lose both the supply ships and the escort
options.consequence: You give up stealth for speed and put the escort between the supply ships and the enemy guns.

costs.resource: the escort tied up out front instead of held back
costs.risk: the enemy spots the fast run, focuses on it, and shatters the group

options.title: Feint a run to fix the picket
advantages: A fake run pulls the enemy to one gap so your real ships use another
It uses the enemy's habit of chasing any run they detect
It can open a clear gap for the cargo that matters most
disadvantages: The decoy ships must show themselves to bait the enemy
If the enemy ignores the fake, they can cover both gaps
It needs two runs to work together, and one run is hard enough
options.consequence: You spend a fake run to clear a gap for the real one, betting the enemy takes the bait.

costs.resource: a decoy run risked to pull the enemy off
costs.risk: the enemy ignores the fake and your real ships run a covered gap anyway

decisionPoints.name: The Last Clean Lane Is Gone
decisionPoints.context: The base needs one more delivery, but the enemy now covers every safe gap. You can push a run through anyway, wait for a new gap that may not open, or send the escort to fight one open.

options.title: Force the contested run
advantages: It gets the cargo to a base that cannot wait any longer
It accepts a risk the short clock has made unavoidable
It meets the garrison's deadline instead of missing it
disadvantages: A run through a covered gap is likely to be caught
You have a high chance of losing supply ships and cargo
The escort may not reach the group in time to save it
options.consequence: You push the run because the base cannot wait for a safer one, and pay whatever the enemy makes you pay.

costs.resource: the whole group risked on a covered gap
costs.risk: the run is caught and the delivery the base needed is lost in the open

options.title: Hold for a gap
advantages: You wait for the enemy's patrol to leave a new gap
You save the group from a run that is close to suicide
A clear gap may still open if the enemy shifts its line
disadvantages: The base's clock may run out before a gap opens
You give up the initiative and just react to the enemy
Waiting is a bet the garrison may lose
options.consequence: You wait for a better moment and bet the base lasts long enough to use it.

costs.resource: time the base may not have
costs.risk: no gap opens in time and the base falls because you held the run back

options.title: Fight a lane open with the escort
advantages: The escort fights an enemy warship to clear a path for the supply ships
It can open a gap that stealth can no longer reach
Driving off an enemy warship makes every later run easier
disadvantages: It sends the escort into a fight against a heavier warship
If you lose the escort, you can no longer run the blockade
A long fight may not clear the gap in time
options.consequence: You send the escort at the blockade to open a path, and bet your one warship on it.

costs.resource: the escort spent on a stand-up fight
costs.risk: the escort is crippled and the group loses both its cargo and its protection

entries.event: The first run launches toward the moon. Your map of the enemy line is hours old and getting worse.
The group slips through its first blind spot. Whether it gets through or is caught sets the pattern for later runs.
The enemy has covered the gap you used, so the next run must take a tighter gap at higher risk.
The base reports its fuel and ammunition. Now you know how many runs you still need against how many gaps are left.
The last safe gaps are gone. To finish the resupply you must run a covered gap, or the base does not make it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Deliver enough to keep the garrison going before the enemy closes the last usable gap. Once no run can get through and the base's reserves are gone, the siege ends without a shot fired on the surface.

opforSketch.composition: This is a {TARGET_FACTION} blockade in space plus a siege force on the ground that your reinforcements must help break. The enemy warships and fighters stay off-table as the threat to each run, and they keep shifting their line to ruin your planning. On the surface, where the 'Mech lander touches down, a siege force of 9-12 medium and heavy 'Mechs (45-75 tons, Regular with a Veteran core) plus some combat vehicles rings the base (vehicleShare covers the siege line's armor and the base garrison's own vehicles). The besiegers press the perimeter and react hard to any landing that could break the ring from inside. The warships and the runs they catch are handled as the blockade threat. The table fight is the surface siege your reinforcements land into.
opforSketch.behavior: The blockade starves the base instead of storming it. The enemy cuts the base off, covers the gaps, and lets time do the work. The surface siege force holds the ring and fights hardest when a landed reinforcement could open it, because a relieved garrison breaking out is exactly what the enemy wants to prevent.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN LANE
forks.trigger: Enough runs get through to carry the garrison past its hold-out clock and the base holds.
forks.consequence: The siege is broken at the supply line; the resupplied garrison holds the moon and {EMPLOYER} keeps the orbital position the blockade was meant to take.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN RING
forks.trigger: The reinforcement lands and the garrison breaks the surface siege, and a picket vessel is driven off badly enough to open a lasting lane.
forks.consequence: The base is not just resupplied but relieved; with a lane held open and the ring broken, {EMPLOYER} can reinforce freely and turn the moon into a base of its own.

forks.name: OPERATION SLACK WATER
forks.trigger: The runs can no longer get through and the base's reserves run out, or the flight is destroyed attempting a contested run.
forks.consequence: The siege ends with the garrison's surrender or destruction; {EMPLOYER} loses the orbital position, and the lighters that survive carry home the knowledge that the fist closed faster than the water could run.

storyElementSeed: A lander pilot holds her ships silent and dark in the shadow of a dead moon. She watches an enemy warship's lights cross the gap she meant to use, and counts whether the next opening comes before the base burns its last hour of fuel.

phases.name: INGRESS — READING THE PICKET
phases.lead: Map the enemy's shifting line from data that keeps going stale, then pick the first gap to run.

dataBlock.Picket: enemy warships and fighters in-system; the line keeps shifting to ruin your planning
dataBlock.Flight: lightly armed supply ships and one 'Mech lander; they cannot fight the enemy warships
dataBlock.Lanes: blind spots, gaps in the debris, and openings in the patrol orbits; there are only so many
dataBlock.Base clock: the base has only a few days of fuel and ammunition left
